In ACC After Dark action, Stanford hosts NC State at Stanford Stadium in Stanford, Calif., on Friday at 10:30 p.m. ET (ESPN). The Wolfpack are 6.5-point road favorites, and my NC State vs. Stanford prediction and college football picks expect CJ Bailey to pick apart one of the Power Four's worst defenses. TOP PICK Who will win NC State vs Stanford: NC State -6.5 Stanford has been completely uncompetitive in four of its last five FBS games and is 1-5 ATS since the start of September. While NC State isn't a powerhouse, the Wolfpack have enough offense to cover up to -8.5 on the road . The Cardinal have lost four of their last five FBS games by at least 28 points and scored seven or fewer in all four (they were outscored 115-10 in their last two FBS games) . With a defense that's ranked 127th in success rate (50.1%) , Stanford's offense won't be able to keep up with the Wolfpack. NC State has scored 31+ points in three of its last four FBS games, all against defenses ranked higher by SP+ than Stanford's (111th). Plus, the Wolfpack are coming off a bye week and should be well rested for the West Coast trip. NC State vs Stanford Over/Under pick: Over 55.5 NC State and Stanford have struggling defenses, which have helped them consistently hit the Over this season. The Wolfpack and Cardinal are a combined 9-4 to the Over, and I like it to hit at 55.5 or better . Stanford's defense has the lowest havoc rate in the ACC (11.3%) and is allowing the second-most yards per game in the Power Four (452) . NC State's defense isn't all that much better, though, ranking 124th in net EPA per play and 133rd in EPA per pass. These two defenses bend and break, ranking the worst in the conference in points per opportunity on defense, though Stanford (5.06) is significantly worse than NC State (3.94). NC State vs Stanford combo Stanford is one of the worst teams in college football, and it doesn't look like Andrew Luck and Tavita Pritchard will be turning things around anytime soon. Though Davis Warren has been efficient at QB, the Cardinal have a dreadful defense that ranks outside the top 115 in EPA per pass, EPA per rush, and available yards percentage (57.3%). Even against an NC State defense giving up 27.7 points per game, Stanford won't be able to keep this close at home against David Doeren's team. The Wolfpack's passing game will be too much, and I have NC State winning 33-24 . The team returned strong with hopes of being the ACC title mix, but everything all but ended in late August with a blowout loss to Virginia. A historically bad play against a lousy Vanderbilt team here, and a 38-14 home loss to a red-hot Wake Forest there, and now the Wolfpack need this. However, win, and there's a chance to go on a big second-half run with a favorable schedule. Stanford is trying to fight the good fight in a rebuild under new head coach Tavita Pritchard, but at 3-4 with only one home game left, it's in big trouble if it loses. NC State vs Stanford: Quick Hits Why does Stanford need this? Three straight road games follow this, but that includes a trip up the road to Cal. NC State only has one game – at Florida State – outside of North Carolina the rest of the way, hosting Cal, Duke, and Syracuse next. The two programs have only met once. NC State beat Stanford 59-28 in 2024. How To Watch NC State vs Stanford Date: Friday, October 23, 2026 Game Time: 10:30 PM ET TV: ESPN Location: Stanford Stadium, Palo Alto, CA – Week 8 Schedule & Predictions – What Will the CFP 12-Seed Bracket Be? – CFN Top 25 | Bowl Projections – CFN Expert Picks: Week 8 Why NC State Will Win When Stanford's offense doesn't work, it really doesn't work. The lack of a pass rush and few defensive stops are the real issues, but you can't win if you don't score, and Stanford can't put the biscuit in the basket. Not to get all basic here, but the Cardinal have scored seven points or fewer in the four losses, and 34 or more in the three wins. The ground game has been non-existent against everyone but Elon and Hawaii. NC State is fantastic at keeping the chains moving. Stanford doesn't get to the quarterback and will struggle to hit Wolfpack star CJ Bailey enough to get off the field. Why Stanford Will Win Okay, context time. Yeah, Stanford's offense was putrid in the four losses. One of those came against a nasty Duke defense Durham, and the other three losses were to Miami, Notre Dame, and a Wake Forest team whose only loss is to the Hurricanes. This is one of those focus-test moments for the ACC team from the Eastern Time Zone. This will end around 2 am NC State time, and while these are college kids who can certainly stay awake, the rhythm will be thrown off. NC State vs Stanford Prediction, Betting Lines Don't just blow this off as a layup win for NC State before getting back on the plane to go deal with bigger and better things. The Wolfpack have had to deal with a whole ton of adversity this season, and they keep coming back, but it's 0-2 on the road, and Stanford is 3-1 at home, with that one loss coming to Miami. NC State doesn't have the pass rush to overwhelm the Cardinal backfield, but it'll be just okay enough to get out with a tough late-night win. Stanford led 14-0 at halftime and 28-0 in the third, before cruising to the easy victory. The Cardinal out gained Elon by a total of 515-272, went 5-12 on third downs, and lost the turnover battle by a total of 1-0 in the game. Davis Warren threw for 279 yards and one touchdown, while JonAnthony Hall caught five passes for 70 yards. Micah Ford rushed 19 times for 179 yards and four scores in the win. NC State Wolfpack Betting Preview The NC State Wolfpack are 3-3 (1-2) this year after they lost to Wake Forest by a score of 38-14 in their last game. away.headline: NC State vs. Stanford injury report update: Duke Scott, Tristan Teasdell, Jojo Trader, Kamen Smith out
away.blurb: The ACC has issued the initial injury report for NC State football vs. Stanford for Friday night in Week 9. Along with the slew of season-ending injuries already known prior to the week, starters Duke Scott and Tristan Teasdell are officially out while Jojo Trader and Kamen Smith are questionable. WEDNESDAY UPDATE: NC State football will officially be without its starting center, right guard and left guard in the trenches against Stanford. Hours after Dave Doeren said on his radio show that guard Kamen Smith was trending toward playing on Friday in Palo Alto, Cal., he was listed as OUT on the Wednesday availability report. Along with Smith, playmaking wide receiver Jojo Trader will also be OUT after missing the last game against Wake Forest due to injury. Trader suffered an apparent lower leg injury in the fourth quarter against Louisville and was trending toward playing Wake Forest, but was held out. Now he'll miss a second straight game when the Pack suits up on Friday. The lone new player to pop up on the injury report was EDGE Harvey Dyson, who was listed as probable. It's rare that Doeren lists players as probable and they don't play, but we'll see what happens. It's been a wild few weeks as far as injuries are concerned, to say the very least. away.blurb: Bailey would have been one of the top quarterbacks available had he entered the transfer portal, but the two-year starter opted to stay put -- a boon for a Wolfpack team looking to build on a strong finish to the 2025 season. The Miami, Florida, native was rumored to be a top target for several schools looking for quarterbacks in his home state, but will return to an NC State team that will now have far higher aspirations following an 8-5 campaign that ended with wins in four of its past five games. Starting QB CJ Bailey returning to NC State for 2026 season - ABC11 Raleigh-Durham 24/7 Live Raleigh Durham Fayetteville Surrounding Area SPORTS NC State will retain starting quarterback CJ Bailey for the 2026 season, he announced on social media. Thrust into the starting role as a true freshman after a season-ending injury to Grayson McCall, Bailey blossomed into one of the more dynamic QBs in the ACC. In 2025, he threw for 3,105 yards, rushed for 215 more, and totaled 31 touchdowns, while leading NC State to a win in Union Home Mortgage Gasparilla Bowl. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect College Football News Transfer Portal 2027 Top Recruits 2027 Top Classes College Football Rankings No. 6 Indiana looks to rebound from a loss to Ohio State, while Michigan begins again at quarterback Getty Images The Tommy Carr era in Ann Arbor will officially get underway this Saturday when the freshman quarterback makes his first career start at home against No. 6 Indiana . Carr led a second-half comeback last week against Penn State after former five-star recruit Bryce Underwood was benched, and Michigan made the decision to fully turn the operation over to Carr against an extremely good Indiana defense. That will present a major challenge for Carr, but it also shows Michigan's faith in him as the best option against the defending champs. Indiana comes into the game trying to shake off the frustration of a loss at home to Ohio State last week, coming a literal foot away from a win had Nick Marsh been able to keep his feet in bounds on a wide-open fourth-down pass from Josh Hoover . The Hoosiers need to refocus after the disappointment of their first loss in two years, as they head into the Big House to face a Michigan team that may not be elite on offense but will still present a stiff test for an Indiana offense that's been out of sync recently. The Hoosiers are 7.5-point road favorites, but the Wolverines suddenly have a bit of life after last week's win, and the excitement for a new quarterback will create a lively atmosphere in Ann Arbor. Michigan vs. Indiana: Need to know Tommy Carr's first start: Carr took over for Bryce Underwood at halftime against Penn State and performed solidly, leading three Michigan touchdown drives -- that came off three Penn State turnovers. While he only threw for 47 yards, playing complementary football and cashing in on great defensive plays to turn them into points is a major step forward for this Michigan offense. However, doing that against a bad Penn State team is one thing; now Carr will face an Indiana defense that's among the best in the country. He'll be tasked with not turning the ball over and taking what's in front of him, but Indiana will know that as well, and Michigan might have to let Carr turn it loose a couple of times down the field if they're going to force the Hoosiers off the line of scrimmage. Michigan knows this will be an extremely difficult first start for Carr and will likely try to protect him with quick concepts and a run-heavy approach, but if they want to pull off the upset, Carr is going to have to deliver a couple big plays Indiana's not expecting. Can Indiana establish a rhythm?: A stop-start offense has been a problem all season for Indiana, and while they escaped the first six games without it costing them, it finally caught up in Columbus. Now they face a Michigan defense that is also excellent and will present plenty of challenges, and Josh Hoover will have to prove he can move the ball consistently through the air. Indiana's offense has been predicated much more on the big play than they'd like this season, as Hoover has been able to create explosives in the passing game to Charlie Becker and Nick Marsh. However, consistency has been lacking, and that's kept the Hoosiers from pulling away from opponents as they did a year ago. Against Ohio State, Hoover threw for 296 yards, but completed just 20 of 40 passes to do so. He will need to figure out how to be sharper in the underneath and intermediate passing game if Indiana's going to have a chance of repeating, and that starts this week given the challenge Michigan will present up front. Elite run defenses: The Hoosiers and Wolverines are two of the nation's best defenses against the run, and that presents real problems for offenses that want to lean on their rushing attacks. Indiana struggled to get anything going against Ohio State, even with Turbo Richard back in the lineup, and they'll be up against it again with a Michigan defense that allows a paltry 2.68 yards per carry. One of the six teams better than Michigan against the run is Indiana, allowing just 2.28 yards per carry, which will put even more pressure on Carr to produce through the air in his first start. The team that can establish some kind of ground game will gain an advantage in this one, but there's a real possibility that neither can break through the walls of these defensive fronts. Where to watch Michigan vs. Indiana live Date : Saturday, Oct. 24 | Time : 12 p.m. ET Location : Michigan Stadium -- Ann Arbor, Michigan TV: Fox | Live stream: Fubo (try free) Michigan vs. Indiana prediction, picks We've got two elite run defenses, one inconsistent passing attack and one freshman making his first start. That is a recipe for a low-scoring battle. Michigan has played five games against teams not named UTEP , and all five games have finished with fewer than 40 points. Indiana's last two games have finished in the 30s as well, as they've faced the two best defenses on their schedule thus far, and it's hard to see a game flow here leading to anything approaching a shootout. The fear here is the potential for defensive scores, but even so, give me the under in Ann Arbor for the second straight week. picks.headline: 3 bold predictions for Indiana football vs. Michigan: Josh Hoover will have a day
picks.blurb: Indiana (6-1, 3-1 Big Ten), for the first time in a long time, is looking to get back on track. It’ll have an opportunity to do just that at Michigan (4-2, 1-2 Big Ten) after falling last week to Ohio State at home. Can the Hoosiers do it ? That would be a hard yes if two of these bold predictions come true and one doesn’t. 3 bold predictions for Indiana at Michigan Michigan doesn’t score a touchdown The Wolverines, despite their abysmal offense through the first half of the season, have scored at least two touchdowns in every Big Ten game thus far. Expect that streak to be snapped by Indiana. The Hoosiers are simply a different test than anything Michigan has seen. True freshman Tommy Carr is poised to get his first career start on Saturday. And while it may be the best decision for the Wolverines, it couldn’t come against a tougher opponent. Indiana is going to speed Carr up, force Michigan to rely on its ground attack and then bottle that up (currently surrendering a Big Ten-best 2.3 yards per carry and just 75.4 total yards per game). The Wolverines might be able to trek into Hoosiers territory on occasion, but never into the end zone. The Hoosiers don’t crack 100 yards on the ground A few signs point in the right direction for Indiana’s run game on Saturday (at least from a total-yardage perspective). First of all, the Hoosiers run the ball a lot – and they’ve been very good at it in the Curt Cignetti era. In Indiana’s first two Big Ten outings, it registered 271 yards and 329 yards on the ground, respectively. Also, against Michigan, the expectation is that the Hoosiers should be leading most of the game. And there is no better way to nurse a lead than run the football. On the flip side, though, Indiana has managed a combined 138 rushing yards on 51 carries over the past two games. The offensive line has failed to get any push and the running backs haven’t been able to find any holes. Chunk plays, explosive plays – the Hoosiers can’t get anything positive (didn’t even have a single rush over 10 yards against Ohio State). The other bad news: Michigan’s rushing defense is elite. It allows just 2.7 yards per carry and 89.7 yards per game. This, unfortunately for Indiana, is a stoppable-force-meets-immovable-object scenario. Josh Hoover throws for three touchdowns Save for the Rutgers win – which, should that even count as Big Ten play? – quarterback Josh Hoover hasn’t thrown for three touchdowns in a league game. That may be set to change on Saturday, though. Michigan’s defense is flat-out dominant. But its lone vulnerability is defending the pass. Iowa’s Hank Brown threw for 227 yards and two scores. Penn State’s Rocco Becht slung it for 267 yards and a touchdown through the air. And, all due respect to both of those gunslingers, but neither is at the same level as Hoover, nor do they have the unreal weapons Hoover has on the outside. Expect Hoover and his stud wide receiver duo of Charlie Becker and Nick Marsh to feast against Michigan, especially considering the ongoing rushing struggles for the Hoosiers’ offense. The Michigan Wolverines got the job done in Week 7 against Penn State, and they're home again in Week 8 in what is one of the toughest games on the regular season schedule for them. If Michigan wants to keep any hopes of being in the College Football Playoff this season, they're going to have to defeat the Indiana Hoosiers on Saturday. Indiana is coming off a narrow loss to Ohio State, but they remain a top-10 team in the country and present a tough task for the Wolverines. Ahead of the game between Michigan and the Hoosiers, the college football staff here at A to Z Sports has some predictions on how this one will go. Indiana 28, Michigan 17 The Hoosiers played well enough to win against an Ohio State team that didn't play well last week, but came up just short. Losing two in a row would be a tough stretch for Indiana, and I don't think it will happen. Charlie Becker confirmed he is one of the best wideouts in the country last week and he's going to present a big problem to Michigan's defense with Nick Marsh on the other side. Michigan's defense is a good unit, but so is Indiana's, and I think it leads to the Wolverines having their defense on the field a ton. Michigan is still going to struggle to put up points with Tommy Carr at quarterback over Bryce Underwood , and it's not going to be enough to beat Indiana. - Brandon Little, A to Z Sports Ohio State Indiana 31, Michigan 20 I know there is a buzz growing in Ann Arbor after the move to Tommy Carr at quarterback, but I don't see a world where Curt Cignetti's Hoosiers drop two in a row after winning 22 straight. The truth is, Ohio State is just a much better football team than Indiana, and the Buckeyes should have won by multiple scores. The same should be true with Indiana and Michigan. I know that Carr will bring optimism, but he hasn't seen a defense like that of the Hoosiers. Not to mention, Josh Hoover and the offense will be looking for a bounce-back performance. I thought Hoover struggled for much of the game against OSU, and obviously everyone has seen Nick Marsh's gaffe at the end. The Hoosiers will be out for vengeance on Saturday. - Rob Gregson, A to Z Sports Alabama Indiana 27, Michigan 10 Indiana was three inches away from coming into this game as likely the No. 1 team in the country and with a ton of momentum and a likely bigger point spread. I don't think three inches changes the fact that they're the far better football team here. Michigan is making a quarterback change, with Tommy Carr taking over for Bryce Underwood. Against IU's deep and talented defense, it won't matter. The Hoosiers stymie Michigan on offense while slowly pulling away in the third quarter. - Craig Smith, A to Z Sports Miami Indiana 31, Michigan 27 This is a really interesting game. The Hoosiers lost in brutal fashion against the Ohio State Buckeyes, and it's very curious how they will respond. They won 22 games in a row, and a national championship, but this team is much different than last year's squad. They also have to contend with a Michigan squad that will be starting a new quarterback, with Tommy Carr starting over Bryce Underwood. That jolt could be enough to keep them competitive, but I don't think it will be enough to get them the win. - Tyler Forness, A to Z Sports Florida Indiana 31, Michigan 17 Indiana jumps on Michigan early and never really lets the Wolverines find their footing, cruising to a 31-17 win behind an explosive passing attack. The biggest storyline heading into this matchup is Michigan's decision to bench Bryce Underwood in favor of true freshman Tommy Carr at quarterback. While the move could eventually pay off, I'm not convinced the transition will be smooth, especially against an Indiana team that has looked capable of making opponents pay for their mistakes. Josh Hoover takes advantage of the matchup, connecting with Charlie Becker and Nick Marsh for several explosive plays that quickly put the Hoosiers in control. Indiana dictates the pace from the opening kickoff, builds an early lead and forces Michigan to play from behind. The Wolverines have enough talent to make things interesting, but asking a true freshman quarterback to step into this situation and keep pace with Indiana is a difficult task. Carr will likely have some growing pains, and the Hoosiers should be able to capitalize on those moments while keeping Michigan's offense from finding a consistent rhythm. Hoover doesn't need to do anything spectacular throughout the entire game, but a few big throws to Becker and Marsh will make the difference. Indiana's ability to establish control early allows it to dictate the game script in the second half, forcing Michigan to take chances offensively. The Wolverines find a way to add some points late, but Indiana's early advantage proves too much to overcome. - Ryan Roberts, A to Z Sports Notre Dame This article was originally published on A to Z Sports. Published Oct. 22, 2026 2:49 p.m. ET share facebook x reddit link Geoff Schwartz FOX Sports Betting Analyst Indiana goes on the road to face the greatest rival of its newest rival, and Utah and Houston will face off in a game that has CFP and Big 12 title implications. On the field, college football is in a great place. Here's what I'm picking in Week 8. This page may contain affiliate links to legal sports betting partners. If you sign up or place a wager, FOX Sports may be compensated. Read more about Sports Betting on FOX Sports . No. 6 Indiana @ Michigan There are two types of wagers for me. There are the kind that I love and those don't tend to cash as often. Then there are the wagers that scare me, and while it is uncomfortable placing said wagers and watching said game, those tend to hit. Wagering on Michigan in this game scares me. Michigan is the right side for many reasons. The first is that Indiana is off its first loss in over a year and a half. How does this squad handle losing at home with all the world watching? And they lost in a way we haven’t seen often — with Curt Cignetti at the helm. Mistakes, turnovers and a receiver just not getting his foot inbounds on the final offensive play of the game cost IU, but the Hoosiers also haven't been able to run the ball this season, which was far from the case last year. It was just 2.8 yards per attempt for their running backs against Ohio State and 2.4 against Nebraska the week before. In addition, Josh Hoover isn’t Fernando Mendoza at quarterback, which we already knew. Hoover can’t make things right like Mendoza could. The Michigan defense is first in yards per play, even though the Wolverines haven't played anyone like Indiana. Still, Michigan’s pass rush is good, and I’d imagine it will try to pressure Hoover into mistakes. It’s also Indiana’s third straight week of playing a physical defense. How do the Hoosiers hold up on the road? I think Indiana’s offense will score in the low 20s. The Indiana defense is still fantastic this season. It is ninth in points per drive and doesn't have many weaknesses. Maybe it allows some success rushing the ball and doesn't rush the passer quite the same as last season. However, it’s still a formidable unit. What worries me the most about this wager is the Michigan offense, which was dead with quarterback Bryce Underwood. Michigan benched Underwood for true freshman quarterback Tommy Carr last week and the offense scored 21 second-half points, appearing competent with Carr under center. However, Carr only threw the ball seven times for 47 yards. Not exactly an elite passing performance. What can Tommy Carr produce for the Wolverines against the Hoosiers? (Getty Images) Now, Carr has to play Indiana’s defense and IU had a week to prepare. I could easily see this Michigan offense being overwhelmed with a true freshman under fire. Still, it is clear the Wolverines are playing more confidently with Carr at QB and I do believe they can score enough, maybe in the high teens, to cover this game. I think I’ll need 17 points from Michigan and I will get it. Schwartz's Pick: Michigan +7 No. 14 Houston @ No. 10 Utah What an awesome Big 12 matchup on Saturday night. The winner of this game has a leg up in the Big 12 title race and a spot in Dallas for the conference championship game. I see a game with points, many of them potentially coming late. But nonetheless, I expect scoring. Utah’s defense has been a hallmark of its program for years, and while it appears to be good this season, I’m not quite sure. It is 26th in yards per play, but the best offense it has faced is 63rd-ranked Kansas, which scored 24 points and passed for 333 yards. Last weekend, Colorado scored 24 points, the most it has scored against an FBS opponent all season. Utah can't rush the passer. It is 66th in pressure rate and 112th in sacks. That's why teams have passed the ball on the Utes. Houston’s offense is well-prepared considering it has already faced Texas Tech on the road and put up 458 yards of offense. The Cougars also just scored 35 against Oklahoma State. Houston’s offensive line is outstanding. It is fifth in rushing success rate and top-25 in pressure rate. The Cougars' offense is first in the sport on third down. Third down has been a strong point for Connor Weigman and the Cougars this season (Getty Images). Houston’s defense is not its strong suit, ranking 99th in yards per play and 124th in percent of plays that go 20+ yards. It is also awful in the red zone, which isn't a great sign against a Utah offense that can attack you in so many ways. The Utes have unique formations and use multiple quarterbacks to run some funky plays. It’s disorienting to go up against. Utah is also seventh in points per drive, great on third down and doesn't allow a ton of QB hits. I think we witness a track meet in Salt Lake City. away.headline: Ohio State QB1 Battle Updated by Ryan Day After Julian Sayin's Injury vs. Indiana
away.blurb: The importance of the quarterback battle extends beyond the Buckeyes' next game against USC, as Day told reporters Tuesday it is "doubtful" Sayin will return for the regular season following his setback in the win over the Hoosiers. Icon Sportswire/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images College Football Ohio State's quarterback battle following Julian Sayin's injury against Indiana will be one of the most consequential storylines of the College Football Playoff race down the stretch of the season, and head coach Ryan Day provided an update Thursday. "Ultimately, I make the final decision, but you take the input from the coaches, take the input from our personnel department and then the players as well," Day told reporters when discussing Luke Fahey and Tavien St. Clair competing for the starting role. "They're the ones in the huddle with these guys. That's what it comes down to." That Day is taking feedback from players is notable, and it's safe to assume one of those players he talks to will be Jeremiah Smith. Smith is arguably the best player in college football, and getting the ball into the hands of the Heisman Trophy favorite will be the most important thing that either Fahey or St. Clair can do when they are under center. Ohio State lost a Heisman Trophy finalist from last year and one of its offensive leaders with the injury. What's more, an already difficult schedule with remaining games against USC, Oregon, Nebraska, Michigan and Northwestern is now all the more daunting without its starting quarterback who completed 68.2 percent of his passes for 2,007 yards, 19 touchdowns and four interceptions prior to the injury. Ohio State Buckeyes - Indiana Hoosiers Highlights 01:26 It may have been something of a surprise for fans heading into the season when Fahey was the backup quarterback and the one who entered games after Sayin exited. After all, he is a true freshman and was a 3-star prospect, per 247Sports' composite rankings. By comparison, St. Clair was a 5-star recruit in the 2025 class, per 247Sports' composite rankings, and has been on campus for far longer. Ohio State turned to Fahey to finish the game against Indiana following Sayin's injury, but the timing of its bye week ahead of the next contest gives Day and the coaching staff more time to evaluate the position moving forward with the context now changed. away.headline: Ohio State survived Indiana, but Julian Sayin's injury may decide the Buckeyes' season
away.blurb: But that stride was debilitating. Marsh's left foot came down out of bounds, and he knew it immediately. The look on his face was heartbreaking. That misery wasn't felt on the Ohio State sideline. Instead, it was relief, but with questions about what's to come. The primary reason Indiana had a chance to win the game late was that Ohio State's starting QB Julian Sayin was knocked out of the game with an apparent right arm injury earlier in the fourth quarter. Ohio State coach Ryan Day said after the game, without going into specifics about the injury, that Sayin would be out "several weeks." The good news is Ohio State is off next week. The bad news is that when the Buckeyes return from their respite, they'll be on the road to face USC , and then it's a home game with Oregon . While both those teams have had their issues in 2026, the prospect of having to face both with a true freshman at QB is not one that should excite anybody in Scarlet and Gray. If Sayin is out even longer, there are games left against a Northwestern team that's now 5-1 after beating Michigan State , as well as a road game against the Nebraska team that gave Indiana fits last week. Oh, and there's Michigan too. College football can be a brutal sport. Sometimes victory can be taken from you by a toe or two; other times, it comes at a serious cost. That was the case Saturday in Ohio State's 19-15 win over Indiana , a game neither team escaped feeling whole. Indiana's 22-game win streak came to an end in an extremely painful manner. Down five late, on a fourth-and-4 at the Ohio State 27, Indiana opted to go for the throat instead of the first down. Josh Hoover dropped back, found a wide-open Nick Marsh down the sideline, and hit him in stride. After taking a vicious hit from Indiana's Mario Landino, Sayin was seen running to the Ohio State locker room, right arm hanging by his side. He emerged a few minutes later with it in a sling, as the diminutive true freshman Luke Fahey filled in for him, and the Buckeyes offense ground to a complete halt. The Buckeyes didn't manage a first down with Fahey in the game, so while they survived the trip to Bloomington, got revenge on the Hoosiers for last season's Big Ten Championship, and avoided a perilous second loss, there are suddenly concerning questions lingering around the program. While Buckeyes fans everywhere celebrate this win, they'll do so while awaiting an injury report that could determine the fate of their season.

Getty Images One week after stunning No. 1 Georgia , Auburn will try to replicate that effort against No. 18 LSU . Auburn will have the Jordan-Hare Stadium crowd on it side, but the team faces an uphill battle in the pursuit of two major upsets. Going into its open date, Auburn was coming off a loss to Tennessee and needed something to build upon. An upset of the No. 1 team in the country on the road will certainly suffice, and now Alex Golesh must find a way to sustain that momentum. If Auburn is going to give itself a shot to slay SEC dragons in consecutive weeks, it will need to put the game on the shoulders of Byrum Brown again. He totaled 265 yards and a pair of touchdowns against the Bulldogs. On the other hand, LSU will have to be wary of entering a hostile environment given its recent history. The team has lost both of its road games this season, and Lane Kiffin's struggles away from home date back to when he first accepted the Ole Miss job. The Baton Rouge-based Tigers just shut out a shorthanded Mississippi State team in Death Valley, and Sam Leavitt played the first clean game of his LSU tenure. He'll need to replicate that performance in Auburn. Before this battle of the Tigers begins, we have everything you need to know about the matchup. LSU vs. Auburn: Need to know LSU's road woes: LSU is the clear favorite in this game, but it has struggled to win road games lately. The Tigers have dropped eight straight road games, which is the third-longest streak in school history. LSU is 0-2 on the road this fall, and Kiffin hasn't fared well away from home throughout his SEC coaching career. Between stops at Tennessee, Ole Miss and LSU, Kiffin is 14-16. Winning on the road is hard, but LSU can't make it even harder. Run, Bryum, run: If Auburn is going to put its best foot forward this weekend -- and for the rest of the season -- Brown will have to use his legs to create offense. That worked last week in Athens, as Brown toted the rock on 26 attempts, which included five sacks. The catch is that Brown will be exposed to more hits, which increases his risk for injury. Because of that, if Auburn can get its traditional run game rolling, that takes some of the workload off Brown's legs. Auburn trying to go back-to-back: Can Auburn pull off two stunners in a row? The Tigers haven't picked up wins over ranked teams in consecutive weeks since they rattled off three straight against Georgia, Alabama and Missouri in 2013. The trouble is that Auburn hasn't played well at home against ranked opponents of late, which is somewhat surprising given the general mystique around Jordan-Hare Stadium. The team is 1-9 in its last 10 home games against top-25 teams. picks.headline: Why this analyst predicts Auburn to lose by double digits against LSU
picks.blurb: The Auburn Tigers are red-hot after their stunning win against No. 1 Georgia last week, but they will not have any time to rest on their laurels, as up next for Alex Golesh’s squad is a big-time matchup with LSU, and early predictions are not in the Tigers’ favor. As it stands, the Tigers are a seven-point underdog to their rival Tigers, though CBS Sports’ Austin Nivison believes the Tigers will lose by at least 10 points . Here’s why. “What Auburn did last week will be commendable -- and fans will remember it forever -- but it was also extremely improbable,” he wrote. “Georgia out-gained Auburn by 74 yards, and the Tigers barely pulled out a win despite a plus-3 turnover margin. LSU's defense is athletic enough to contain Brown, and the offense is capable of putting up big numbers. It's possible the crowd and Auburn defense give Sam Leavitt trouble, but LSU is capable of winning this game by double digits.” In fact, every CBS analyst polled about the game took Lane Kiffin’s squad to win straight-up, but a few, like Chip Patterson and David Cobb, predicted the Tigers to at least cover the spread. It’s certainly a difficult matchup for the Tigers, who could be experiencing what Kiffin called ‘relief syndrome’ after their win against Georgia. There is a path to the Tigers winning this game, though, and it seems to run through Byrum Brown. “If Auburn is going to put its best foot forward this weekend -- and for the rest of the season -- Brown will have to use his legs to create offense,” Nivison continued. “That worked last week in Athens... The catch is that Brown will be exposed to more hits, which increases his risk for injury. Because of that, if Auburn can get its traditional run game rolling, that takes some of the workload off Brown's legs.” Brown seemed to have been contained a bit in earlier games, as his number was called for design plays quite rarely, but against the Dawgs, Auburn offensive coordinator Joel Gordon leaned on Brown’s legs to get the Tigers’ offense moving. It worked to great effect last week, but LSU will now be even more prepared for Brown’s dual-threat nature, which adds a layer of complexity to the Tigers’ playcalling this week. The Tigers, coming off a marquee win, are looking to continue their momentum, and having home-field advantage should play a big part in their matchup with Kiffin’s Tigers. However, LSU has answers for most of Auburn’s offensive production, so the Tigers will likely need to get creative if they want to emerge from the Tiger Bowl with a win. The LSU Tigers bring the country's best opponent-adjusted net EPA profile to Jordan-Hare Stadium, while the Auburn Tigers still need Byrum Brown to manufacture too much of the offense himself. I'm laying the points with LSU and grabbing the Under as my best bet in this Tigers vs Tigers affair. Head over to our latest college football picks for more Week 8 betting analysis. Who will win LSU vs Auburn: LSU -7.5 I would play the LSU Tigers to 50%. Last week's win over the No. 1 Georgia Bulldogs absolutely raises the Auburn Tigers ' ceiling, but it took 26 Byrum Brown carries and three Gunner Stockton turnovers to pull it off. Additionally, Auburn is coming off one of its biggest wins in recent memory. I'm not here to tell you that LSU is a better football team than Georgia, but its profile may be more suitable for this matchup. The visitors sit No. 1 nationally in opponent-adjusted net EPA per play at +0.44 , while Auburn is 35th at +0.14. Brown is Auburn's engine on the ground, yet he ranks 100th among qualifying quarterbacks in EPA per dropback. That's a dangerous imbalance against a defense that can crowd the box and still trust its coverage. Jordan-Hare will have some real juice too, with belief injected into Auburn's season. However, LSU's down-to-down edge should create separation over 60 minutes. TOP PICK LSU vs Auburn Over/Under pick: Under 51.5 The Under is my top pick in this matchup and I'd play it to 49.5. Brown is producing 0.41 EPA per rush, fourth among qualified runners, and a heavy quarterback-run plan is the best way to keep the game close . That also bleeds clock. LSU's defense has held opponents to 4.35 yards per play and a 39.2% success rate, while Auburn's unit ranks 31st in adjusted EPA allowed and gives up 5.15 yards per snap . LSU's offense is good, but its opponent-adjusted efficiency ranks 25th rather than among the elite. Also, I still have not seen enough from Sam Leavitt to trust him to make game-defining plays. I don't think his head coach has either. LSU can control field position and reach the low 30s. Auburn landing in the teens leaves enough room for Under 51.5. LSU vs Auburn combo The prevailing theme throughout is LSU's defense. It controls the game, wins the game for the Tigers, and keeps it low-scoring throughout. That holds true early on, which is why I added the first-quarter Under to this combo beyond the previously mentioned two plays. I don't expect either team to come out guns blazing through the air due to decision-making concerns tied to the quarterback. That's particularly true early in the game when the emphasis on either to score quickly is minimal. That should keep the clock running most of the first quarter and start off this heavily correlated combo out strong. Can the Auburn Tigers pull off another upset in year one under head coach Alex Golesh? Auburn pulled off the biggest upset of the college football season by defeating No. 1 Georgia this past Saturday in Athens. Now, they turn their attention to the LSU Tigers as a team with confidence that has proven they can beat anyone. Auburn enters this game as the underdog. The ESPN Matchup Predictor gives Auburn a 28.8% chance to win. Auburn will need to play the type of game they did in the win over Georgia. They will need to control the line of scrimmage and be consistent at running the football. Auburn outgained Georgia 192-113 on the ground. The LSU Tigers rank No. 1 in the conference, allowing just 88.1 yards per game on the ground. However, the Bulldogs rank No. 2 in that category, and Auburn had success with Byrum Brown and the running backs. The turnover battle will be key once again. Auburn forced three turnovers against Georgia and did not commit any of their own. Going into that game, interceptions had been an issue for Brown with seven on the season. Auburn will be facing a quarterback in Sam Leavitt who has thrown eight interceptions this season. The Auburn defense will need to create opportunities for the offense to gain an upset victory. A big advantage for Auburn is that they are playing at home. Both of LSU's losses were away from Baton Rouge, at Ole Miss and at Kentucky. The crowd at Jordan-Hare should be electric on Saturday after Week 7's upset win at Georgia. Pete Fiutak Thu, October 22, 2026 at 6:12 AM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads All of a sudden, the SEC is up for grabs, and Auburn and LSU had a lot to do with that. Ten SEC teams fall into the 4-1 to 2-2 range after Auburn pulled off a stunning 27-24 win at Georgia last week. The rest of the AU Tiger schedule is challenging, but if you can beat Georgia in Sanford Stadium, the bar gets set a little higher. LSU lost both of its road games – Ole Miss and Kentucky – but it's been an unstoppable force at home, destroying Clemson by 41, Texas A&M by 29, and beating Mississippi State 31-0 last week. The Bayou Bengal Tigers are still among the most dangerous and talented teams in the country on the right day, but, like Auburn, one more loss and that's about it for the SEC and College Football Playoff dreams. LSU vs Auburn: Quick Hits LSU gets a nasty run over the next three games, but Alabama and Texas are home games before going to Tennessee. Auburn goes to Ole Miss next, and three of the last four SEC games are on the road. LSU beat Auburn 48-18 when the two last met in 2023 and has won six of the last eight games. How To Watch LSU vs Auburn Date: Saturday, October 24, 2026 Game Time: 12:00 PM ET TV: ABC Location: Jordan-Hare Stadium, Auburn, AL – Week 8 Schedule & Predictions – What Will the CFP 12-Seed Bracket Be? – CFN Top 25 | Bowl Projections – CFN Expert Picks: Week 8 Why LSU Will Win LSU has to take the fight to Auburn right away, but without getting caught up in the tempo. The Auburn offense wants to move at a lightning-fast pace, and Lane Kiffin's attack is at its best when it's going 150 miles per hour. The one big difference is control of the tempo. LSU is amazing at dominating the time of possession battle, and it should hold the ball for large chunks of time. Auburn is 133rd in the nation, keeping the ball for fewer than 27 minutes per game. As much as the offense matters, though, it's the LSU defense that has to keep Auburn from getting out of third gear. LSU is second in the nation in sacks, and AU can't keep quarterback Byrum Brown from getting popped. Why Auburn Will Win It really is impressive. LSU looks and plays like it has 14 guys on the field who are all twice as fast as everyone else … at home. The LSU offense wasn't too bad in the losses to Ole Miss and Kentucky, but the defense occasionally played like it didn't attend the last three classes before the test. It's not a coincidence. LSU has allowed more than 145 passing yards just two times this season. Take a wild guess which teams got it going through the air. In case you were wondering, the 21-15 win over Vanderbilt is the only time Auburn failed to throw for at least 145 yards. LSU vs Auburn Prediction, Betting Lines Let's get it out of the way. It wasn't funny when the line was first written in 1999, and it's even more brutal now, but college football is nothing without its traditions, so … "This is our five-star, all-time, can't-miss lock of the century for this week … the Tigers are going to win." Really, how did Auburn beat Georgia? First of all, Auburn is just that good. But also, it actually held its own in the time of possession battle – the defense held up and wasn't gassed late. That, and it helped to get be +3 in turnover margin. LSU quarterback Sam Leavitt will throw his customary interception – although he didn't give one away for the first time all year in last week's win over Mississippi State – but LSU's control of the clock and the narrative on the lines will be enough to finally get a road win. away.blurb: LSU football expects to have its pass rusher available when the Tigers travel to face Auburn on Saturday. LSU defensive end Princewill Umanmielen was absent from the Wednesday injury report, a good sign after Umanmielen left LSU's win over Mississippi State and did not return. LSU's defense was already dealing with the injury bug. Defensive back Da'Shawn Spears tore his ACL vs. Ole Miss and will miss the entire season, while linebacker Whit Weeks is missing an extended period and won't return until November. If LSU were without Umanmielen, the Tigers would be down yet another impact player. LSU managed fine after Umanmielen left the Mississippi State game, going to win 31-0, but LSU's defensive end depth is a question mark, and Umanmielen is an All-American-caliber player. LSU's pass rush is elite with Umanmielen on the field. Umanmielen has eight sacks and 22 pressures in 2026. He also makes an impact against the run, with six run stops this year. Umanmielen was a key piece of LSU's transfer portal class and was with Lane Kiffin at Ole Miss. LSU faces Auburn this Saturday at 11 A.M. CT. home.blurb: LSU football expects to have its pass rusher available when the Tigers travel to face Auburn on Saturday. LSU defensive end Princewill Umanmielen was absent from the Wednesday injury report, a good sign after Umanmielen left LSU's win over Mississippi State and did not return. LSU's defense was already dealing with the injury bug. Defensive back Da'Shawn Spears tore his ACL vs. Ole Miss and will miss the entire season, while linebacker Whit Weeks is missing an extended period and won't return until November. If LSU were without Umanmielen, the Tigers would be down yet another impact player. LSU managed fine after Umanmielen left the Mississippi State game, going to win 31-0, but LSU's defensive end depth is a question mark, and Umanmielen is an All-American-caliber player. LSU's pass rush is elite with Umanmielen on the field. Umanmielen has eight sacks and 22 pressures in 2026. He also makes an impact against the run, with six run stops this year. Umanmielen was a key piece of LSU's transfer portal class and was with Lane Kiffin at Ole Miss. LSU faces Auburn this Saturday at 11 A.M. CT. The 5-2 Tigers need a win to keep their College Football Playoff hopes alive. This article originally appeared on LSU Wire: LSU football DE Princewill Umanmielen on track to play vs Auburn

picks.headline: ‘Tennessee just went to war last week against Alabama' – ESPN's Greg McElroy predicts the final score of Tennessee vs South Carolina matchup
picks.blurb: ‘Tennessee just went to war last week against Alabama' – ESPN's Greg McElroy predicts the final score of Tennessee vs South Carolina matchup - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Lendeborg shades Luka Canes' murky ACC future Reese, Dream win Game 3 Ant spoils Giannis' Heat debut World Series preview Randy Sartin-Imagn Images Zach Ragan Tue, October 20, 2026 at 4:52 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Tennessee Volunteers will travel to Columbia this weekend for a matchup against the South Carolina Gamecocks. Tennessee is facing one of its scariest tests of the season this weekend. After dominating Alabama last weekend in Knoxville, the Vols are set to head to Columbia this weekend for a matchup against South Carolina. It's a classic trap game for Tennessee in a stadium that's been a house of horrors for the program over the last two decades (the Vols are just 2-6 in Columbia since 2008, and one of those wins came in 2020 when fan attendance was limited due to Covid). South Carolina is coming off a bye week after a big road win against Florida earlier this month. ESPN's Greg McElroy picks winner of Tennessee vs South Carolina ESPN's Greg McElroy, who called the Vols' win over Alabama last weekend, thinks Tennessee will falter in Columbia on Saturday. McElroy has South Carolina beating Tennessee 27-24. "Can South Carolina stop the run that keeps Tennessee on schedule?" said McElroy. "Tennessee has 46 runs of 10 or more yards. That's top nine in the country, and Josh Heupel's teams are 71-9 when they run for 150 yards or more. Look, South Carolina is pretty stingy on those runs. So this is strength against strength, and the pick kind of tilts on whether Tennessee's quarterback can hold up his end of the bargain. "I'm going to take South Carolina to win this game 27-24. I think they're going to win on the ground. They're also coming off a bye. Tennessee just went to war last week against Alabama. They looked amazing doing it, but we've seen teams elevate and then come back to earth the following week, and I think that could happen for Tennessee right here. Because (Matt) Fuller and (LaNorris) Sellers are going to get yards when that first defender misses. Tennessee's linebackers cannot afford to miss in this game. So that (Fuller and Sellers) will keep the Gamecocks out of third and long — which is where Tennessee's sacks live. It shrinks those pass rushing opportunities that are Tennessee's very best weapon." "Tennessee's defense is amazing," added McElroy. "They're sixth in points per drive. They're gonna make this thing super tight. But I just lean towards the Gamecocks in this game and the potential flat spot for the Volunteers — even though they bring the better defense into the matchup. The Gamecocks bring a run game and receivers that can win one-on-one. So we will take the Gamecocks." Vols fans won't love that pick, but it's hard to blame McElroy, who has been pretty accurate with his predictions this season, based on Tennessee's past history in Columbia. Tennessee and South Carolina will kick off at 3:30 PM ET on Saturday. The game will air on ESPN. This article was originally published on A to Z Sports. Everyone is expecting the Vols to come out flat after their big win against Alabama and have a letdown game against the Gamecocks. Former Georgia quarterback Aaron Murray is picking South Carolina to win . So is former Alabama quarterback Greg McElroy . Another former SEC star who is picking South Carolina is David Pollack, a former Georgia standout. Pollack has the Gamecocks winning 27-20 on Saturday. It's breaking tackles and making extra plays." "What South Carolina can do through the passing game is create some explosive plays off of the run game, and because of that, they finally get their finish," added Pollack. I think it's a good game, but I also think South Carolina is really talented, and that's a tough place to play. South Carolina wins by seven, 27-20." picks.headline: Can Tennessee football avoid letdown at South Carolina, other SEC picks | Adams
picks.blurb: Can Tennessee football avoid letdown at South Carolina, other SEC picks | Adams - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Lendeborg shades Luka Canes' murky ACC future Reese, Dream win Game 3 Ant spoils Giannis' Heat debut World Series preview Can Tennessee football avoid letdown at South Carolina, other SEC picks | Adams John Adams, Knoxville News Sentinel Wed, October 21, 2026 at 9:06 AM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Georgia's Kirby Smart has won so much for so long that he's regarded as the best coach in college football . But after a last-second loss to Auburn, he proved he can also be one of the sport's best quotes. "Humility is a week away," he said. Tennessee coach Josh Heupel would be wise to paraphrase Smart's comment before the Vols take on South Carolina at Williams-Brice Stadium in Columbia. The Vols are coming off a dominant 26-10 victory over Alabama . They're 6-1 and on the cusp of the top 10. But all they gained from a victory over their archrival could be lost with a loss to the unranked Gamecocks. Tennessee 26, South Carolina 16: In an unpredictable SEC season, team performances have varied drastically from one Saturday to the next. Based on that trend, Tennessee could be next in line to take a tumble after a big win. But amid all the SEC's inconsistency, UT's defense has remained steadfast. Something else to consider: Tennessee has been coming on strong in the second half; in South Carolina's last five SEC games dating back to last season, it has lost leads of 27, 16 and 17 points. LSU 31, Auburn 23: While I believe Tennessee's defense will prevent a letdown against South Carolina, I'm not as confident about Auburn's chances for prosperity after upsetting No. 1 Georgia. The LSU offense hasn't always been the model of consistency, but neither has Auburn's. LSU's challenge: Winning on the road. It already has lost at Ole Miss and Kentucky. That's a carryover from the Brian Kelly era. The Tigers lost all four of their SEC road games in 2025. They also lost their last two conference road games in 2024. So, they will take an eight-game SEC road losing streak with them to Jordan-Hare Stadium. They're due. Alabama 30, Texas A&M 15: The Tide also are due for a win after losing back-to-back games against Georgia and Tennessee. They can be grateful that their schedule offers a home game against the three-loss Aggies, who have lost two SEC games by 21 or more points. Texas A&M's 41-0 victory over The Citadel hardly qualifies as the beginning of a turnaround. However, it at least demonstrated that the Aggies aren't devoid of young talent. Freshman running back KJ Edwards led Texas A&M with 116 yards rushing on 16 carries. Freshman wide receiver Aaron Gregory led the Aggies' injury-depleted receiving corps with six catches for 94 yards. Oklahoma 23, Mississippi State 20: This matchup is all about quarterbacks. You can't be sure if Bulldogs quarterback Kamario Taylor is healthy enough to play. Without him, Mississippi State lost 31-0 to LSU. With him, it scored 38 points against Minnesota and 41 on South Carolina. The health of Oklahoma quarterback John Mateer isn't an issue. Performance is his problem. Mateer is a fiery competitor and a running threat. But he doesn't protect the football. He has lost two fumbles and thrown seven interceptions in six games. And he has thrown only two more touchdown passes than interceptions. In Mateer's last season at Washington State (2024), he threw seven interceptions in 12 games. He also threw 29 touchdown passes. Texas 30, Ole Miss 27: The Longhorns are getting less for their NIL money than any other program. But just because you have a big-bucks payroll doesn't mean you have a big-play offense. Texas has scored fewer than 24 points in four of its six games. ADAMS: Tennessee football should be well aware of South Carolina threat on road And the Longhorns are on the verge of playing themselves out of the playoffs for a second consecutive season. But they might be catching the Rebels at the right time. A week after beating LSU, Ole Miss lost to Florida by 28 points. Now, it's coming off a 28-point victory over Missouri. Kentucky 34, Vanderbilt 23: You might conclude that after five consecutive victories, the Wildcats are about to learn, as Smart said, that "humility is a week away." As accurate as Smart's assessment might be in general, it doesn't apply if you're playing Vanderbilt. Record: 59-14 (.793), 48-26 (.642) against the spread. John Adams is a senior columnist. (Sam Wolfe/Special To The State) Michael Sauls Thu, October 22, 2026 at 11:00 AM UTC · 6 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads South Carolina football is back in action this weekend. Shane Beamer and the Gamecocks will face No. 11 Tennessee at Williams-Brice Stadium on Saturday. The SEC matchup is set to kick off at 3:30 p.m. and will be televised on ESPN. South Carolina (3-3, 1-3 SEC) is coming off a bye week but knocked off ranked Florida on the road for its first SEC win on the road on Oct. 10. Tennessee (6-1, 3-1 SEC) enters Saturday's matchup ranked No. 11 in the country after beating rival Alabama last week. Tennessee leads the all-time series against South Carolina 29-11-2. The Volunteers beat the Gamecocks 41-20 in 2023, the last time the two teams faced each other. South Carolina rolled to a 63-38 win over Tennessee in 2022, the last time the two teams played in Columbia. From 2012-2020, eight of the nine matchups between the SEC rivals were decided by six or fewer points. Each of the last three games have been decided by double-digit margins. Here's what you need to know about Saturday's game: South Carolina vs. Tennessee football game on TV Who: South Carolina (3-3, 1-3 SEC) vs. No. 11 Tennessee (6-1, 3-1 SEC) When: 3:30 p.m. Saturday Where: Williams-Brice Stadium Stream: Disney+, ESPN app or ESPN.com Broadcast crew: Wes Durham, Dusty Dvoracek, Taylor McGregor Local radio crew: Todd Ellis, Tommy Suggs, Chet Tucker Satellite radio: Sirius XM channel 176 or 229 (953 on app) Series history: Tennessee leads all-time series 29-11-2 (UT won last matchup in 2023). South Carolina vs. Tennessee betting odds The sportsbooks out in Vegas have had a change of heart on this game in recent days. Tennessee initially opened as a 2.5-point favorite to win the game, per the VegasInsider Consensus. But as of Wednesday, the line has swung in favor of the Gamecocks. South Carolina is currently a 2.5-point favorite, per popular sportsbooks like DraftKings and FanDuel. The Gamecocks are currently 2-4 against the spread this season. While the spread is now in favor of USC, ESPN still favors the Volunteers. ESPN Analytics gives South Carolina a 40.1% chance to beat Tennessee. Cotton candy alert The South Carolina State Fair is in town. Gamecock fans who are making the trip to Williams-Brice Stadium on Saturday should account for extra traffic as a result. Injury updates South Carolina had six players listed on the official SEC injury report released Wednesday night. WR Jayden Sellers, EDGE Kobby Sakyi-Prah, OL Josiah Thompson and OL Seth Smith are all listed as out. Thompson and Sellers are both out for the year. Two starters are listed on the report in DB Quay'sheed Scott and OL Carter Miller. Scott is listed as doubtful and Miller is listed as questionable. Both missed the Florida game. The SEC injury report will be updated on Thursday, Friday and 90 minutes before kickoff on Saturday. Weather forecast for the game in Columbia For the first time this season all signs point towards it being perfect football weather in Columbia on Saturday. The forecast is supposed to be "pleasant with plenty of sunshine," per AccuWeather . The high is set to be 70 degrees and the low is 50 degrees. There will be some wind and just a 1% chance of precipitation at Williams-Brice Stadium on Saturday. Top storylines Feeling like 2024? This won't be the first time in Beamer's tenure the Gamecocks have entered a pivotal matchup with a 3-3 record. In 2024 , South Carolina was 3-3 and beat a solid Oklahoma team on the road. It was the first of six-straight wins (four of which were against Top 25 teams) to close the season and got USC to the playoff bubble. The vibes feel similar coming into Saturday's matchup with Tennessee, especially after USC's upset win over a ranked Florida team two weekends ago. Will a win this week start a potential playoff run for the Gamecocks again this year? Only time will tell. Run vs. run: Saturday's matchup will feature the two best rushing offenses in the SEC . South Carolina is No. 1 in the league with 232.33 yards per game and Tennessee is No. 2 in the league with 217.14 yards per game. Both have star running backs — Matt Fuller for USC and DeSean Bishop for Tennessee — and strong offensive lines. USC's rushing attack was weaker than usual last time out against Florida, and will need to get back to its usual ways if it wants to outrun the Vols. Tennessee's QB conundrum: Not even Tennessee head coach Josh Heupel knows who will start at quarterback for the Vols on Saturday (at least that's what he said Monday). Freshman Faizon Brandon started the first five games of the year for Tennessee but hasn't played since Oct. 3. He totaled 697 yards, seven touchdowns and one interception in that time. Sophomore Georgie MacIntyre has played in six games this year but started the last two. He's thrown for 592 yards, two touchdowns and three interceptions this year but led UT to a win over Alabama last week. Beamer and his players said the Gamecocks are preparing for both quarterbacks. South Carolina and Tennessee players to watch South Carolina QB LaNorris Sellers: South Carolina's QB1 has looked more like himself in recent weeks. After totaling six touchdowns and four interceptions in USC's first four games he's thrown six touchdowns and no interceptions in the last two games. Sellers was named SEC Co-Offensive Player of the week for his 299 total yards of offense and five total touchdowns against the Gators. South Carolina EDGE Caleb Herring: Herring gets a crack at his former team on Saturday. The senior started his college career at Tennessee. In three years, Herring played in 36 games for the Vols and totaled 25 tackles and five sacks. He's made a big impact for the Gamecocks since transferring this season. Herring is essentially a co-starter at edge and has totaled eight tackles and two sacks. Tennessee RB DeSean Bishop: Tennessee's starting running back might have one of the best stories in college football. Bishop was a star at nearby Karns High School and his lone major offer was from the Vols. He joined the team as a walk-on and missed his freshman season with an injury. Bishop was put on scholarship in the spring of 2025 and ran 1,076 rushing yards and 16 touchdowns for Tennessee last season. He was the first Tennessee player in nearly a decade to record over 1,000 rushing yards. Through eight games this year he's No. 2 in the SEC with 837 rushing yards and 10 touchdowns. Tennessee LB Amare Campbell: The senior has paced the Tennessee defense so far this season. Campbell has 46 total tackles in 2026. That's the most by any player on the team and ranks 16th in the SEC. He's coming off a game in which he had eight tackles, including two tackles for loss, in a win over Alabama.

This season, he is among the top players on the roster with NFL interest. During training camp, Klein said he hosted several NFL scouts who were on campus to check out Oakley. Here's Latest Injury Update On Kansas State Wildcats TE Garrett Oakley - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAB Ant spoils Giannis' Heat debut Here's Latest Injury Update On Kansas State Wildcats TE Garrett Oakley (USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect) Shandel Richardson Tue, October 20, 2026 at 3:50 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads The Kansas State Wildcats are expected to once again be without one of their key offensive players this weekend on the road against the Arizona State Sun Devils. K-State coach Collin Klein hinted that tight end Garrett Oakley could miss the third game of the Big 12 conference schedule. Oakley did not play in last week's game against the Kansas Jayhawks in the Sunflower Showdown at Bill Snyder Family Stadium. Here's what Klein had to say during his weekly press conference about the Oakley situation. "Probably unlikely, but we'll see," Klein said. "Day to day." Oakley missed the game because of an undisclosed illness. It gave more opportunities to sophomore Linkon Cure, who is among the most hyped players in program history. He is the first five-star recruit to ever play at Kansas State. While he has gotten off to a slow start, the Wildcats are hoping he can live up to the huge expectations. He has seven catches for 66 yards this season. Last week he caught two passes for 16 yards. The Wildcats need production from Cure because Oakley isn't the only tight end missing. Two weeks ago, it was announced that backup Will Anciaux would miss the season after sustaining a lower leg injury. Klein is also experimenting with moving left tackle Oliver Miller to tight end. That's where he played last week in the win against the Jayhawks. It is unknown if the move is permanent but that's where Miller will play this week. This was a move that was in the works because the Wildcats coaching staff was using him at tight end the past few weeks. A 6-foot-6 freshman, Miller has embraced the opportunity. He was a standout at Cherry Creek (Colo.) High School, where he was rated the No. 41 tackle in the country. Perhaps this could be a better calling for him because of his athleticism. The hope is Oakley is back in uniform sooner than later. He is a big component of the offense and is needed if the Wildcats are going to remain in the hunt for the Big 12 conference championship and College Football Playoff.

Memorial Stadium should be sold out this weekend, and Swinney will look to continue the strong stretch coming out of the open date. However, when looking at the advanced analytics, it could mean that Clemson has to survive a strong test from the Hokies to pick up its third ACC win of the season. Fortunately for fans, there tends to be a lean towards the Tigers in that department, according to Versus Sports Simulator . It gives Clemson a 64% chance to win on Saturday, with an average score being around 29-23. This contest has been one that has constantly switched in the projections, due to the losses that both teams have had since the month of October began. Virginia Tech had a two-game skid against Pitt and Cal, losing by a score in both games, to be forced to win out for the remainder of the season. However, when the month began, the Tigers only had a 53% chance to win. The model gives Swinney’s group a defense with a B+ grade, while the offense is generously given a B- grade. That’s how Clemson has won games over the course of this season, with the defense leaving enough points on the board for the Tigers to score on sporadic occasions. On the flip side, Virginia Tech is given a C+ overall ranking by Versus, with its best quality being a B- offense. However, it’s important to note that the Hokies’ defense, although graded a C+, leads the country in tackles for loss and is also first in the ACC in sacks and forced fumbles. Regardless, Clemson is expected to hit the ground running, with this amount being the most it has scored against a Power Four opponent at all this season. The home-field advantage plays a small factor in the Tigers' favor, with betting markets having them favored by about a field goal. Even with the game being at Memorial Stadium, Versus has Clemson as the favorite regardless of where the game is. If the game were at Lane Stadium, Swinney’s group would have a 52% chance to win the game on Saturday. However, there’s much more to a game than the model itself, but the advanced analytics show advantages on Clemson’s end that perhaps others aren’t thinking about. Swinney will look to reinforce that at home on Saturday, playing a team that will be playing with hopes to remain in the ACC Championship contention pool. Kickoff is set for 7 p.m. and the game will be broadcast on ESPN. picks.headline: ESPN predicts the winner of Clemson football vs. Virginia Tech
picks.blurb: Virginia Tech's Ethan Grunkemeyer leads the Hokies into Memorial Stadium, less than a year after he squared off against the Tigers in the Pinstripe Bowl at Yankee Stadium while playing for Penn State. In that game, Grunkemeyer threw for 260 yards and two touchdowns in Penn State's 22-10 win over Clemson. A third-year QB who committed to the Nittany Lions and James Franklin, Grunkemeyer followed his former Penn State coach to Blacksburg after Franklin was hired by Virginia Tech last November after the Nittany Lions parted ways with the 12-year skipper barely a month earlier. He has thrown for 1,984 yards and 15 touchdowns to two interceptions through seven games this season. Grunkemeyer and Virginia Tech lead the ACC in passing yards , though the Hokies have played one more game than Darian Mensah and the No. 1-ranked Miami Hurricanes. Clemson's passing game has been a complete contrast, to say the least. Through their first six contests, the Tigers have thrown a combined two touchdown psases between Week 1 starter Christopher Vizzina and former four-star freshman Tait Reynolds. The Tigers are second to last in the ACC in total offense with 340.7 yards per game while Virginia Tech ranks sixth (449.7) in the conference. Reynolds was 17 of 26 for 127 yards in Clemson's 37-0 win over Charleston Southern in Week 6. He has thrown for 943 yards with one touchdown and three interceptions entering his fifth start of 2026. Will Clemson football beat Virginia Tech? ESPN's prediction Oddsmakers have Clemson as a 2.5-point favorite over Virginia Tech, but as always, ESPN Analytics has its own odds for Saturday's game. ESPN's matchup predictor , which offers a prediction model based on its college football power index and other variables, gives Clemson a 55.9% chance to win. Virginia Tech has a 44.1% chance. The Tigers are No. 48 in ESPN's FPI with a 6.5 rating, which ranks 10th among ACC teams. Virginia Tech has a 6.6 rating that's one spot ahead of Clemson in ESPN's metrics. The Tigers are one spot ahead of Oregon State (6.0) in the FPI. Clemson football has longshot odds of reaching ACC title game entering Week 8 In ESPN's FPI entering Week 8, Clemson's chances of reaching six wins to qualify for a bowl game stand at 88.4%. The Tigers' chances of winning the ACC, however, are just 0.3%. That's down from 0.9% before the Tigers' 41-13 loss to the Miami Hurricanes on Oct. 3. Clemson's chances of reaching the 12-team College Football Playoff are 1.5%, which is down from 4.1% prior to the Miami loss and down from 22.2% entering the season. ACC football teams ranked by ESPN FPI: Who is best suited to beat Miami? There's a big gap between Miami and the rest of the ACC, but here is where Clemson and all 17 conference teams rank in ESPN's FPI: 17. Stanford Cardinal (-11.4 FPI) 16. California Golden Bears (-3.9 FPI) 15. Boston College Eagles (-2.6 FPI) 14. Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets (0.3 FPI) 13. Syracuse Orange (0.5 FPI) 12. NC State Wolfpack (1.1 FPI) 11. Virginia Cavaliers (5.6 FPI) 10. Clemson Tigers (6.5 FPI) 9. Virginia Tech Hokies (6.6 FPI) 8. Duke Blue Devils (7.8 FPI) 7. North Carolina Tar Heels (8.7 FPI) 6. Pitt Panthers (9.2 FPI) 5. Florida State Seminoles (9.6 FPI) 4. SMU Mustangs (9.8 FPI) 3. Louisville Cardinals (13.3 FPI) 2. Wake Forest Demon Deacons (15.4 FPI) 1. Miami Hurricanes (26.5 FPI) What are ESPN FPI ratings? ESPN explains: "The Football Power Index (FPI) is a measure of team strength that is meant to be the best predictor of a team's performance going forward for the rest of the season. 4 bold Virginia Tech predictions for Saturday night's primetime showdown at Clemson
picks.blurb: After breaking a two-game losing streak at home with a win over Georgia Tech last weekend, the Virginia Tech football team will hit the road this Saturday night for a key ACC battle at Clemson in a battle between a pair of two-loss teams. It'll be the first of three difficult road games remaining on the schedule in James Franklin's first season in Blacksburg. The Hokies will have home games next month, with Stanford and Virginia sprinkled in. Here are four bold predictions for Virginia Tech's primetime showdown in Death Valley. 4 Bold Virginia Tech football predictions for Clemson primetime showdown Virginia Tech scores 20-plus points This could end up being a low-scoring game, and some Clemson fans believe that the Tigers need to keep the Hokies under 20 points to have a realistic shot at winning. Virginia Tech has scored at least 20 points in every game this season, and Clemson has a stout defense. However, you have to think that Virginia Tech finds a way to break the 20-point plateau. It might not seem like a bit of a bold prediction, but the way the Tigers play defense and being on the road under the lights at Memorial Stadium, it is. Virginia Tech's defense forces multiple turnovers You have to think that Brent Pry's defense will build off of getting two takeaways last week against the Yellow Jackets and get multiple turnovers this week. If they want to have a shot at pulling off the upset, they will have to. Clemson's offense has sputtered at times this season, and getting off the field with some turnovers would go a long way toward securing an upset on the road. Turnovers both ways are going to play a big part in the outcome. Luke Reynolds records another 100 yards plus receiving Clemson coach Dabo Swinney spoke this week about Hokies tight end Luke Reynolds and how good he is. He got an up-close look at him last season in the Pinstripe Bowl when Penn State defeated the Tigers at Yankee Stadium. Clemson is going to know where Reynolds is on the field and look to shut him down, but that doesn't mean they will. Look for Hokies offensive coordinator Ty Howle to get him targets and for the future NFL tight end to make some big catches. Davion Brown records a touchdown reception Swinney spoke very highly of Reynolds and wide receiver/punt returner Que'Sean Brown this week, and it wouldn't be surprising to see the Tigers focus on them. While we believe that Reynolds will still have a big game, if they focus too much on Que'Sean Brown, that opens things up for freshman Davion Brown, and don't be surprised to see quarterback Ethan Grunkemeyer target him a little more often. He made an outstanding one-handed catch against Georgia Tech last week and should see more balls thrown his way this weekend. Virginia Tech will need a wide receiver or two to step up, especially if the running game struggles. The final availability report is out for this game, and it includes the final status for running back Justice Haynes, who was listed as doubtful coming into Saturday, as well as offensive lineman Josh Petty and defensive lineman Landen Marshall. RB Justice Haynes and OT Josh Petty are going to be game-time decisions. If Haynes is unable to go today, Trelain Maddox and Chad Alexander would be the top options in the backfield for the Yellow Jackets today against Virginia Tech. Maddox is coming off the best game of his career last week against Duke. Riggs, the Yellow Jackets starting center, came back from an injury last week in the win over Duke, but was hurt during the game and did not return. He was not on the injury report this week and should be starting in the middle of the Yellow Jackets offensive line against what has been one of the ACC's best defensive fronts through the first part of the season.
