LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect College Football News Transfer Portal 2027 Top Recruits 2027 Top Classes College Football Rankings Texas is looking to end a two-game skid and get its College Football Playoff hopes back on track against an Ole Miss team coming off its best performance of the year so far Getty Images Arch Manning grew up with Ole Miss all around him. His uncle Eli's jersey was retired in Oxford, and so was his grandfather Archie's No. 18. On Saturday night, Arch faces the Rebels for the first time, possibly at the lowest point of his career. Questions have swirled around Arch during a two-game losing streak that has the Longhorns on the brink of falling completely out of the polls after rising to No. 1 in September with a comeback win against top-ranked Ohio State . He threw two interceptions, including a pick-six, in the loss to Oklahoma , and last week he lost a fumble on a strip sack with two minutes remaining, allowing Florida to hold on for a win, Manning's first home loss as a starter. Afterward, Sarkisian said he would evaluate the offense, including Manning's role in the offense. Now Texas (4-2, 1-2 SEC) is trying to avoid joining 1965 Texas and 1957 Texas A&M as the only teams to lose three straight games in a season after entering as the AP No. 1 team. The Longhorns will be without the nation's sacks leader, Colin Simmons , who has a high ankle sprain. No. 7 Ole Miss (5-1, 3-1) has won two straight by a combined 63 points and has redisovered its groove following a 28-point win against nationally-ranked Missouri last week. Ole Miss vs. Texas: Need to know Arch Manning's evaluation : Manning is expected to start Saturday, but how short will the leash be? Backup KJ Lacey has gotten more first-team reps over the last two weeks, fueling speculation he could step in against the Rebels. Manning threw only seven interceptions in 13 games last season. He's up to five picks through six starts this season. "He's our starter, but I need to see a better version of Arch Manning like I need to see a better version of a lot of guys on our offensive football team right now, but we need to see a better version of him this week," Sarkisian said. Life without Colin Simmons : Simmons leads the FBS with 10.5 sacks and 16 tackles for loss. He had eight tackles, four TFL and a sack against Florida before he was carted off in the fourth quarter, and reports have him out three to four weeks. That's a problem against Ole Miss quarterback Trinidad Chambliss , who has thrown a touchdown pass in 19 straight games, tied for the second-longest streak in Ole Miss history. His 20 total touchdowns rank second in the SEC, and Ole Miss leads the FBS in red zone touchdown percentage (87.5%). Ole Miss rebuilt itself after Florida : The Rebels left Gainesville in September after a 52-28 loss Golding called an "old-fashioned butt whooping." The Gators ran for 302 yards, and Ole Miss managed one tackle for loss and no sacks. Since a bye week, Ole Miss beat Vanderbilt 52-17 on the road and Missouri 31-3 at home. Kewan Lacy (122 yards) and Makhi Frazier (101) both topped 100 yards against the Tigers. The road remains the question. Ole Miss is 1-10 in its last 11 road games against ranked SEC teams, and Golding's lone road game as head coach against a ranked opponent was the loss at No. 21 Florida. Kewan Lacy comes home : Lacy grew up in Dallas as a Texas fan, and dreamed of playing for the Longhorns, but they never offered the running back a scholarship. "I can't wait to see them," Lacy said this offseason. He has 29 career rushing touchdowns, third in school history and the most in the SEC since 2025, though Golding has managed his workload since he missed the Florida game. His 13-game rushing touchdown streak ended against Missouri, but he still ran for a season-high 122 yards. Where to watch Ole Miss vs. Texas live Date : Saturday, Oct. 24 | Time : 7:30 p.m. ET Location : Darrell K Royal-Texas Memorial Stadium -- Austin, Texas TV : ABC | Live stream : Fubo ( try free ) Ole Miss vs. Texas: prediction, picks Texas is a 2.5-point favorite, and the SportsLine model projects a 29-17 Longhorns win. History backs it. Ole Miss is 1-6 straight up and against the spread as a road underdog against ranked teams since 2020, and Texas has won three straight home games against top-10 opponents. But is this the same Texas team that has been so successful at home? The Longhorns scored 17 points against a Florida defense that ranked last in the SEC, and the Gators sacked Manning five times with 11 tackles for loss. Texas hasn't scored more than 24 points against a power opponent. The offensive line is a mess, ranking 111th in sacks allowed, and the running game is subpar at 101st. The Longhorns are also 1-5 against the spread this season and haven't covered five straight. Ole Miss has the better quarterback and a run game that just went for 257 yards. Without Simmons, Texas loses the one defender built to wreck Chambliss' night. Texas also lacks championship-level coaching. TOP PICK Who will win Ole Miss vs Texas: Texas -3.5 Archie Manning never played against Texas, but Arch Manning has the chance to lead the Longhorns to their first win against his grandfather and uncle's alma mater since 2012. According to former UCLA head coach Rick Neuheisel, Texas will need to make key adjustments to its strategy ahead of the upcoming game. "He's good enough, he's athletic enough, he's smart enough, and for a 22-year-old, he has handled this pressure so well." They shut down Missouri cold. [Missouri] couldn't do anything on the ground. Ole Miss dominated them on the ground. You still have Trinidad Chambliss. I still might take him No. 1 overall from a quarterback perspective. Running back Kewan Lacy is healthy. Their defense is right. Their star players are back, and as good as Texas' defense is they did struggle in the second half. They, as Sarkisian put it, kind of bled out and couldn't get a stop as DE Colin Simmons left that game with an injury. It's unclear whether he's going to return. Even if he does, he left on a cart. I can't imagine that he would be 100% even if he is on the football field. And now you've got to run around and defend Trinidad Chambliss? I don't love that at all. "I think Ole Miss wins this outright, 28-21. I'll take the -3.5 and take Ole Miss." Klatt's straight-up pick: Ole Miss Klatt's pick against the spread: Ole Miss +3.5 Utah 30, Houston 27 Devon Dampier and Utah pulled out a close 27-24 win over Colorado in Week 7. (Photo by Bryan Byerly/ISI Photos/ISI Photos via Getty Images) Spread: Utah -6.5 Moneyline: Utah -225, Houston +185 Klatt's thoughts: "Houston at Utah. How about an underrated Houston win last week. Houston with a great performance, particularly out of their quarterback, Conner Weigman. They beat Drew Mestemaker and the Cowboys 35-32 in a great game. You know how I feel about Mestemaker. I think he's one of the better quarterbacks in the country. Houston's for real. I know that they lost that game earlier this year [against Texas Tech]. But man, they can throw the football, their defense can stop the run. Weigman is having a great season, he's second in the country in touchdown passes and total touchdowns. He's playing at a very high level. They've got two wide receivers that I like a lot, Amare Thomas and Trent Walker ... Now [Houston] has to go on the road and face Utah, who is historically very good at home in Salt Lake. I don't love how Houston played on the road against Colorado. "I didn't love what I saw from Utah. They faced a lot of lower-level competition, both from Power Four and otherwise to start, and they were hammering lower-end opponents. Then they face a few opponents with a pulse, like mid-Kansas and Colorado. They end up getting the wins, but in both of those games it's in doubt in the second half. As much as you know, I love Utah, I didn't even have them in my top 10. They still have Devon Dampier, they still have Wayshawn Parker. They should still be able to run the ball. But, Houston can stop the run. I think Utah could struggle to stop some of the run game against Conner Weigman and these two wide receivers. I see a bit of a higher scoring game. "I see Utah ultimately winning because of the home field. But I have to take the 6.5 towards Houston in this one. Utah wins it 31-27." Klatt's straight-up pick: Utah Klatt's pick against the spread: Houston +6.5 LSU 34, Auburn 30 Can LSU and Lane Kiffin avoid a road loss this season in its Week 8 showdown at Auburn? (Photo by Tyler Kaufman/Getty Images) Spread: LSU -7.5 Moneyline: LSU -298, Auburn +240 Klatt's thoughts: "LSU at Auburn. LSU is favored by 7.5 Auburn coming off of that huge win over Georgia. LSU routed Mississippi State 31-0. Remember, Mississippi State was without Kamario Taylor in that game, he was banged up, didn't play. At Auburn, I think you've got to look at LSU on the road and what they have been not only this year but in the recent past. LSU struggles on the road. They're 0-2 this year on the road. So, that needs to change for Lane Kiffin. Their defense needs to play well, obviously, because Byrum Brown has back-to-back 100-yard rushing games from the quarterback position, and that is the formula for Alex Golesh and Brown. "Like, I don't think Auburn is just going to get stomped out by LSU. They both have two losses, and 7.5 on the road is too much, not for a team that has lost their last six on the road. Now, I think LSU gets the win, but that's too many, so I've got to take the 7.5. I think LSU wins this 34-30. I'm going to take the 7.5 for Auburn. "I know it's an emotional win, and we have seen teams this year after emotional wins really have a letdown. I'm going to bank on the fact that [Auburn is] returning home and getting to play at home, and LSU's got to go on the road. I'm banking that Golesh is going to get Brown going on the edge a little bit. We'll see if LSU's defense can react. LSU is banged up. Lane Kiffin's lamenting the [nine-game conference schedule]. He's trying to throw excuses in front of his team." Klatt's straight-up pick: LSU Klatt's pick against the spread: Auburn +7.5 USC 24, Wisconsin 20 Jayden Maiava currently leads the Big Ten in passing yards with 2,045. (Photo by Joe Robbins/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) Spread: USC -2.5 Moneyline: USC -155, Wisconsin +130 Klatt's thoughts: "USC at Wisconsin. USC favored by 2.5 on the road, coming off of a bye week. Their last matchup was on the road against Penn State in the whiteout. Wisconsin was on the road last week in L.A., getting beat by UCLA in a 17-7 game. I'm really interested to see what that Penn State win did for USC. Their confidence on the road, their overall operation on the road. We have seen them struggle mightily, in particular going east. Even this year when they tried to go out to Rutgers, they got the win but it was sloppy, in particular on the defensive side. Then they go out there and they get the win over Penn State. And Wisconsin was able to beat Penn State also at Penn State. I think this could be a close game. "[USC has] got Trent Mosley back on the outside. They're getting a little healthier after the bye week. I just think that even if you're playing great defense, they're still going to score 21, 24 points. They should be able to run football a little bit. Wisconsin's not great against the run; they're okay, but not great against the run. I like what Luke Fickell has done. I am a big fan of this Wisconsin team, but they can't throw the football. Colton Joseph is a good, solid running quarterback, but they cannot throw the football. If that's the floor for USC, the only way Wisconsin gets there is if USC props them up. So Jayden Maiava's got to play clean. They can't turn the football over. You can't have special teams gaffes. And if they can play clean from a penalty perspective, I know that's a huge if, huge if. I think USC is able to go out there and get the win on the road, even in a close game, and even in a close win. "You've got to have them covering the 2.5. USC, 24-20 in this ball game." Klatt's straight-up pick: USC Klatt's pick against the spread: USC -2.5 Iowa 24, Minnesota 17 Jeremy Hecklinski led the Hawkeyes to a 41-24 win over Washington in his first start for Iowa. (Photo by Steph Chambers/Getty Images) Spread: Iowa -6.5 Moneyline: Iowa -258, Minnesota +210 Klatt's thoughts: "Iowa at Minnesota. Iowa is ranked 15th, they're favored by 6.5. They're playing really well. They blew out Washington and Seattle the last time we saw them play. I like Minnesota. I love P.J. Fleck . How are they scoring 17 against Iowa in this game? I don't see it. Meanwhile, they're not stopping the run. Purdue ran for over 300 yards on the ground against Minnesota last week. Don't love that aspect of what's going on. "So here we are with Iowa. They're going to run the football. They're going to play great defense. They're Iowa. I actually like Jeremy Hecklinski at quarterback, maybe even over Hank Brown. Their only loss was against Ohio State in a game in which Jeremiah Smith was going off and nobody on the planet could defend him. I think this is a team that's going to be there in the end in the Big Ten. You look at their schedule: it is manageable. I like Reece Vander Zee, their wide receiver. I like Hecklinski. I like their tight end. Their defense is always good, and again, that rush defense from Minnesota just scares me. After Purdue was able to get after them on the ground, maybe the defense against Michigan was more about Michigan than it was against Minnesota. "I'm going to go Iowa in this one. I think that they cover the 6.5, even on the road, something along the lines of, you know 24-17." away.headline: Three Ole Miss offensive linemen on injury report, but there’s reason for optimism
away.blurb: Ole Miss has some personnel questions heading into Saturday night's showdown at Texas, but one part of Wednesday's SEC availability report stood out more than anything else. Three starting offensive linemen appeared on it. Starting left tackle Terez Davis and center Brycen Sanders were listed as questionable, while right guard Patrick Kutas was listed as probable. The good news for Ole Miss is there's no reason to believe any of the three are in serious danger of missing the game. Kutas, especially, would be a surprise absence given his probable designation. Sanders returned to last week's 31-3 win over Missouri after leaving with an injury, and while Davis didn't come back, he remained on the sideline in uniform. Still, it's hard to ignore seeing three starters from the same position group show up on the report before a road trip to Austin. The concern isn't necessarily whether they'll play. It's the fact Ole Miss is entering one of its biggest games of the season with questions along the offensive front. As for Kewan Lacy, his inclusion feels far less significant. Lacy was listed as probable after briefly leaving last week's game with a hamstring issue, but he still ran for 122 yards against Missouri. At this point, it wouldn't be surprising if his name appears on most injury reports the rest of the season as Ole Miss manages the situation. The bigger story remains the offensive line. If the Rebels have all three starters available Saturday night, they'll likely feel good about where they stand. But heading into a hostile road environment against a talented Texas defense, it's a group worth monitoring. Colin Simmons' absence would be a big break for Ole Miss While Ole Miss is watching the health of its offensive line, Texas appears likely to be without one of the nation's premier pass rushers. EDGE Colin Simmons was listed as doubtful after suffering an ankle sprain in last week's loss to Florida. That designation aligns with reports earlier this week indicating Simmons is expected to miss multiple weeks. Barring a surprising turnaround, it would be unexpected to see him on the field Saturday. That's significant for Ole Miss. Simmons leads the nation with 10.5 sacks and has been the centerpiece of the Texas pass rush. The Longhorns also listed EDGE Richard Wesley as out, further impacting their depth up front. Texas still has plenty of defensive talent, so this isn't a matchup-changing development by itself. But for an Ole Miss offensive line dealing with multiple injury concerns, potentially avoiding the nation's leading sacker is about as favorable a piece of injury news as the Rebels could have received this week. Texas will face perhaps college football's best quarterback Saturday when Ole Miss ' Trinidad Chambliss comes to Austin. The Longhorns (4-2, 1-2 SEC) will likely do so without their best defensive player. This video created with the assistance of AI. Simmons' exit against Florida halted his statistical climb and hindered the Longhorns defense. The examination reportedly revealed no structural damage, providing some encouraging news regarding his recovery. The junior defensive standout required assistance leaving the field before eventually being transported to the locker room on a cart. Before exiting, Simmons had delivered another impressive performance, recording eight tackles, four tackles for loss and one sack. His absence represents a substantial blow to a Texas defense that has relied heavily on his ability to disrupt opposing offenses. picks.headline: Vanderbilt defense preview: Kentucky offense can dominate
picks.blurb: Vanderbilt defense preview: Kentucky offense can dominate - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Lendeborg shades Luka Canes' murky ACC future Reese, Dream win Game 3 Ant spoils Giannis' Heat debut World Series preview Story by Wildcats Wire Vanderbilt defense preview: Kentucky offense can dominate Braxton Howard, UK Wildcats Wire Wed, October 21, 2026 at 4:14 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Kentucky football will host Vanderbilt under the lights at Kroger Field on Saturday night, as it is the final game before the Wildcats enter a much needed bye week. The first College Football Playoff rankings will happen in two weeks after the Wildcats bye week, and there is a great chance we see Kentucky on the graphic if they can improve to 7-1 against Vanderbilt. There shouldn't be any extra motivation needed, as a lot of these players remember the beatdown that happened in Nashville last season when Vanderbilt defeated Kentucky 45-17 in a blowout fashion. Kentucky has an opportunity to return the favor on Saturday, as the Commodores have one of the worst defenses in the SEC. Vanderbilt is struggling in a lot of ways on the defensive side of the football, and Kentucky's offense should be able to capitalize. The Commodores rank last in the SEC in pressure rate and tackle for loss rate, they have had a difficult time of forcing negative plays. Vanderbilt also allows the highest success rate in conference, and Kentucky ranks fourth in the SEC in offensive success rate. The real key to watch in my opinion is early down conversion rate and third down conversion rate, Vanderbilt's defense allows the highest percentage to opponents in the SEC; Kentucky's offense is one of the best in the country at converting on early downs and they have a chance to improve on third downs this weekend. There are a few players to watch on Vanderbilt's defense, and we will get more into that when we release our X factors for the game. It starts up front with veteran edge defender Miles Capers and defensive tackle Issa Ouattara who is a massive 6'7, 305-pound lineman that clogs up the middle. On the back end, senior safety CJ Heard is a player who plays in the box and can make plays all over the field; Heard is dangerous as a blitzer, he is a sure tackler and is probably the best player on the team in coverage. However, there is a stark contrast in this defense compared to the one the Wildcats just faced in Oklahoma. Vanderbilt has allowed 121 total points in their last three games against Georgia, Ole Miss and Arkansas. The Commodores are allowing 40 points per game over the last three weeks. This is probably the worst defense left on Kentucky's schedule. This creates a perfect opportunity for the Wildcats to get things going offensively to improve to 7-1 heading into the bye week. Vanderbilt has the lowest pressure and tackle for loss rate in the SEC, as previously mentioned, so this is a game where all eyes are on the Kentucky offensive line. This is a game they should dominate, they can get movement in the running game and keep Minchey clean for 60 minutes. Vanderbilt is allowing over four yards per carry and 146 rushing yards per game. You have to wonder if the coaching staff keeps CJ Baxter out of this game to get him to the bye week so he is as close to 100% as possible for the final stretch; this could be another heavy Jason Patterson and Jovantae Barnes game. Kentucky has yet to put together four quarters of football where they are firing on all cylinders. I think this is the game we could see that play out, specifically from an offensive standpoint. Now that the Wildcats are in the thick of the College Football Playoff hunt, how you win in these games can matter to a degree. Kentucky needs a dominant win on Saturday to keep that momentum going into the bye week. picks.headline: Vanderbilt offense preview: Kentucky can win in trenches
picks.blurb: Vanderbilt offense preview: Kentucky can win in trenches - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Lendeborg shades Luka Canes' murky ACC future Reese, Dream win Game 3 Ant spoils Giannis' Heat debut World Series preview Story by Wildcats Wire Vanderbilt offense preview: Kentucky can win in trenches Braxton Howard, UK Wildcats Wire Wed, October 21, 2026 at 6:38 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Kentucky football will try to keep to momentum rolling as they enter their bye week after they host Vanderbilt under the lights on Saturday. Kentucky just played one of the best defenses in the SEC in Oklahoma , and now they get to play one of the worst as we previewed the Vanderbilt defense . On the offensive side of the football, the Commodores are led by five star true freshman quarterback Jared Curtis. The offense has struggled but Curtis has shown plenty of flashes although he has a ton of room to grow. In our Vanderbilt defensive preview, we really centered it around Kentucky's offense and how they can exploit the Commodores defense. We are going to do the same here because this game is about Kentucky staying focused to enter the bye week with a 7-1 record. Jared Curtis has a rocket for an arm and is a big, physical runner. Kentucky head coach Will Stein said that Curtis plays like Josh Allen, but he made it clear he was not making the comparison. Coach Stein is correct though, Curtis can make unreal throws down the field and runs with physicality that is rare at the quarterback position. However, Curtis has a long way to become the dangerous player he is capable of. Curtis still needs to fix little things like footwork, staying in the pocket and taking care of the football. Curtis has one of the highest turnover worthy play percentages in the SEC, he will put the ball in harms way against this Kentucky defense that has been incredibly opportunistic this season. Curtis does not have much help around him, his offensive line has struggled all season. Vanderbilt allows the highest pressure rate in the SEC, which has led to Curtis being sacked a total of 10 times this season. However, Curtis is really difficult to bring down with his 6'4, 230-pound frame. His ability to erase sack opportunities is similar to South Carolina's LaNorris Sellers. Kentucky will win this matchup in the trenches, this deep defensive line unit will be able to get consistent pressure on Curtis. The biggest question will be how often they can convert those pressures into sacks, which they have been better at doing the last two weeks against Sam Leavitt and John Mateer. It will be a vital coaching point all week for the Wildcats to finish the play and get Curtis on the ground. If they allow Curtis to extend plays with his legs and erase sacks, it can lead to big plays down field as a passer or scrambling for a first down. Luckily for Kentucky, they won't have to see wide receiver Tre Richardson as he transferred to Louisville. Richardson lit them up last year down the field with Diego Pavia throwing all over this defense. I am sure a lot of the returning Wildcats on the defense have not forgotten that 45-17 beatdown last year in Nashville. This motivation will play a factor against a Vanderbilt team that is in a rebuilding stage. The Commodores receiving room is led by veteran Junior Sherrill, who is far and away the best weapon on this offense. Sherrill leads Vanderbilt in receptions, yards and touchdowns. He has four touchdowns on the season and all other wide receivers have combined for just one on the season. This is the guy to watch when Vanderbilt is on offense, they will force feed him the football. Vanderbilt offensive coordinator Tim Beck has one of the most unique offenses in the country and we saw how dangerous it could be last season. However, they lost their quarterback Diego Pavia who thrived in his system, they also lost their mismatch tight end Eli Stowers and the explosive weapon Richardson who transferred to Louisville. This is very much a transition year for this offense and it shows up on film. Kentucky has another opportunity to make a statement on defense after creating four turnovers and holding Oklahoma to just one touchdown last week. Kentucky Football continues to climb in the AP Top 25 Poll , moving up three spots to No. 12 after defeating Oklahoma, 21-13, in Norman. The Wildcats improved to 6-1 overall, became bowl eligible, and strengthened their hopes of reaching the College Football Playoff in head coach Will Stein’s first season. The victory was far from perfect, as Kentucky’s offense struggled to find consistency after an impressive opening drive. However, the defense came up with several crucial plays down the stretch to help the Wildcats secure another impressive road win. Kentucky’s offense looked sharp on its opening possession, slicing through Oklahoma’s defense and setting the tone early. However, the unit stalled after that drive and did not score another offensive touchdown until 12:53 remained in the fourth quarter, when quarterback Kenny Minchey connected with Willie Rodriguez for the Wildcats’ second touchdown of the game. Although the final score was relatively low, Kentucky’s defense also struggled at times in the first half. Safety Jordan Castell came up with a key interception when Oklahoma attempted a fake field goal in the first quarter, ending a promising Sooners possession. The Wildcats’ defense began to turn things around late in the third quarter when Ty Bryant intercepted Oklahoma quarterback John Mateer, giving Kentucky possession in Sooners territory. From there, the defense took control. Oklahoma recorded two three-and-outs and threw two more interceptions. Castell returned one for a pick-six, extending Kentucky’s lead to eight points, while Bryant secured the game-ending interception to seal the victory. While the game was sloppy on both sides, Kentucky found a way to finish strong. The Wildcats improved to 6-1, earned bowl eligibility, and continued building momentum as they pursue a potential College Football Playoff appearance. Now, Kentucky returns home to Kroger Field to face Vanderbilt, looking to avenge consecutive losses to the Commodores while losing three of four in the series. Kentucky fell 45-17 on the road last season after suffering a 20-13 defeat at home the year before. With Vanderbilt struggling through a disappointing season, the Wildcats will have an opportunity to extend their winning ways and continue climbing the national rankings. But if this last weekend showed us anything, it’s that upsets are commonplace this season, and Kentucky can’t afford to come out flat against a Commodores team starving for its first SEC win of the season. That, and Vandy did nearly pull off an upset over an Auburn team that just won at No. 1 Georgia. The Dores may be struggling, but they’ve still got an SEC roster. Vanderbilt Commodores (3-4, 0-4 in SEC) Vanderbilt has struggled through the first seven games of the season, and life after former quarterback Diego Pavia has been challenging. The Commodores finished the 2025 regular season with an impressive 10-2 record before losing to Iowa in the Citrus Bowl, ending the year at 10-3. However, the Dores have not come close to replicating that success this season. Vanderbilt suffered a disappointing 31-21 loss to Arkansas this past weekend. The Razorbacks entered the matchup on a 14-game Southeastern Conference losing streak, but they snapped that drought against the Commodores. One of Vanderbilt’s biggest challenges has been the development of 5-star true freshman quarterback Jared Curtis. The young signal-caller has shown flashes of his talent, but his inexperience has been evident. The drop-off from Pavia to Curtis has been noticeable, and Vanderbilt’s decision to start a true freshman at quarterback has come with growing pains. Through seven games, Curtis has completed 101/161 passes for 62.7%, totaling six passing touchdowns and seven interceptions. He has also been sacked 11 times. Curtis measures 6-foot-3 and weighs 230 pounds, giving him the physical tools to develop into a quality quarterback. He can also make plays with his legs, recording 55 carries for 144 rushing yards and two touchdowns. However, his turnover numbers and struggles under pressure will be areas Kentucky looks to exploit. Vanderbilt’s other major weakness has been its defense, particularly against the run. The Commodores have struggled to establish consistency along their front seven, which could create problems against Kentucky’s rushing attack. The Wildcats have a three-headed backfield featuring CJ Baxter, provided he is healthy enough to play, alongside Jason Patterson and Jovantae Barnes. If Kentucky can keep all three involved, Vanderbilt could have a difficult time slowing down the ground game. Kentucky’s offensive line, known as the Big Blue Wall, has also looked impressive this season. If the unit continues to open running lanes and control the line of scrimmage, the Wildcats could have a significant advantage. As for Vanderbilt’s offense, Curtis has several weapons at his disposal. Senior wide receiver Junior Sherrill has emerged as Curtis’ primary target. The 5-foot-11, 200-pound receiver has recorded 41 receptions for 628 yards and four touchdowns so far this season. Junior wide receiver Ja’Cory Thomas provides another option at 6-foot-3 and 215 pounds. He has recorded 12 receptions for 195 yards and one touchdown. Vanderbilt also features junior tight end Jayvontay Conner, who stands 6-foot-4 and weighs 235 pounds. Conner has totaled 13 receptions for 146 yards, though he has yet to score a touchdown this season. Junior receiver Tristen Brown has added another option in the passing game, recording 12 receptions for 145 yards. In the backfield, Vanderbilt relies primarily on two running backs. Senior Sedrick Alexander, who stands 5-foot-9 and weighs 207 pounds, has recorded 61 carries for 270 yards and five touchdowns. Senior Makhilyn Young, at 5-foot-10 and 210 pounds, has added 52 carries for 216 yards and two touchdowns. For Vanderbilt to pull off the upset, Curtis will need to protect the football, make better decisions under pressure, and find ways to move the ball against Kentucky’s defense. The Commodores will also need to improve against the run to keep the Wildcats’ offense from controlling the game. Kentucky, meanwhile, will look to establish the run early, protect Minchey, and continue creating turnovers defensively. With the Wildcats playing at home and Vanderbilt struggling in SEC play, Kentucky has an opportunity to deliver another convincing win against a team that’s had its number. ESPN gives Kentucky an 85.4% chance of winning. Our Early Prediction: Kentucky enters this matchup at 6-1 and bowl eligible, with its attention now turning toward the College Football Playoff. Under first-year head coach Will Stein, the Wildcats have shown they can win in different ways, whether through explosive offensive performances or clutch defensive plays in lower-scoring games. Vanderbilt, meanwhile, is reeling after falling to 3-4 overall and 0-4 in SEC play. Losing to Arkansas after the Razorbacks had endured a 14-game conference losing streak raises further questions about the direction of the Commodores’ season. Kentucky also has extra motivation after losing to Vanderbilt in each of the past two seasons. With the Wildcats playing at home, an improving defense, and a rushing attack capable of taking control of the game, I expect Kentucky to avenge those losses and earn a convincing victory. picks.headline: How No. 12 Kentucky football and Vanderbilt match up — with a game prediction
picks.blurb: • Kentucky’s Kenny Minchey completed 21 of 28 passes for 158 yards and two touchdowns in the Wildcats’ 21-13 win at Oklahoma last week. The 6-foot-2, 211-pound transfer from Notre Dame has been a paragon of efficiency so far as a Wildcat. On the season, Minchey has completed 68.4% of his throws for 1,551 yards with 13 touchdowns vs. one interception . • Vanderbilt true freshman Jared Curtis is a player UK coach Will Stein sought to recruit while serving as Oregon offensive coordinator. “He’s very young,” Stein said of Curtis, “but in terms of the tangibles of the position, being able to throw it, arm talent, running strength, he is a prototype first-round-type talent.” A homegrown, 6-3, 230-pound Nashville product, Curtis is completing 62.7% of his throws for 1,242 yards and six touchdowns. Ball security has been an issue for the freshman QB, who has thrown seven interceptions and lost two fumbles. Advantage : Kentucky Running backs • Kentucky leading rusher CJ Baxter (484 yards, 5.6 yards a carry, eight touchdowns) sat out last week’s victory at Oklahoma with an undisclosed injury. In Baxter’s absence, third-year player Jason Patterson led UK with 38 yards on 12 carries vs. the Sooners. Former Oklahoma back Jovantae Barnes carried five times for 16 yards last week vs. his former team. • Vanderbilt coach Clark Lea deploys a two-man running back rotation. Senior Sedrick Alexander has run for 270 yards and five touchdowns and is averaging 4.4 yards a rush. The 5-9, 207-pound product of Austin, Texas, has also caught 11 passes for 94 yards and a score. Senior Makhilyn Young has rushed for 232 yards and two TDs and is averaging 4.2 yards a carry. A 5-10, 210-pound product of Midland, Texas, Young has caught 10 passes for 76 yards. Wide receivers • Kentucky’s Kenny Darby was named a Midseason Freshman All-American by On3 Sports this week. The 6-1, 180-pound product of Bossier City, Louisiana, leads UK with 34 catches and 436 receiving yards and is tied for the team lead with three touchdown receptions. Senior Nic Anderson made an acrobatic, juggling catch against Oklahoma — the team for whom he played as a freshman. Over the past three games, the 6-4, 205-pound Atlanta product has caught 13 passes. On the season, Anderson has 17 catches for 197 yards and a TD. • Vanderbilt senior Junior Sherrill is fourth in the SEC in receptions with 41. A 5-11, 200-pound Nashville product, Sherrill has 628 receiving yards and has caught four touchdown passes. In Vandy’s 45-17 strafing of UK last season, Sherrill caught eight passes for 115 yards and a TD. Advantage : Even • Kentucky’s Willie Rodriguez is putting together an All-SEC-caliber season. The 6-4, 249-pound, third-year player from Covington Catholic High School caught five passes for 38 yards and two touchdowns in last week’s win at Oklahoma. On the season, Rodriguez has 33 catches for 257 yards and three TDs. • A transfer from East Carolina who began his college career at Ole Miss, Vanderbilt’s Jayvontay Conner has 13 catches for 146 yards. Cole Spence has six receptions for 72 yards. In last season’s blowout of UK, Spence caught three passes for 48 yards. Offensive line • Kentucky left offensive tackle Lance Heard was named a First Team Mid-Season All-American this week by On3 Sports. A 6-6, 325-pound product of Bonita, Louisiana, Heard was recently ranked the 29th-best prospect for the 2027 NFL draft by CBSSports.com. • Vanderbilt “quick guard” Cade McConnell is the only returning starter along the offensive front from last season’s 10-3 team. A 6-5, 323-pound product of Choctaw, Oklahoma, McConnell began his college career at Minnesota. Center Lyndon Cooper logged 25 career starts at Pittsburgh and was considered a portal-recruiting coup for Vandy. Advantage: Kentucky Defensive line • Kentucky end Mi’Quise Humphrey-Grace and tackle Tavion Gadson were disruptive forces for UK late in the win at Oklahoma. Humphrey-Grace, a 6-4, 271-pound senior from Cincinnati, was credited with 1.5 sacks and three quarterback hurries vs. the Sooners. It was Humphrey-Grace deflecting the ball off the throwing hand of Oklahoma QB John Mateer that set up the Ty Bryant interception that was the turning point in the game. Gadson, a 6-5, 303-pound junior from Savannah, Georgia, made eight tackles, 1.5 sacks and broke up a pass. “Those guys are really good players,” Will Stein said of Gadson and Humphrey-Grace. • At 6-7, 305 pounds, Vanderbilt tackle Issa Ouattara is an impactful presence in the interior of the Commodores’ defensive front. A product of Cologne, Germany, Ouattara has two sacks and three QB hurries so far in 2026. Edge Miles Capers leads Vandy with six tackles for loss and has two sacks, an interception and the forced fumble that set up Vanderbilt’s game-winning touchdown on the final play of a 35-31 victory over North Carolina State. • Kentucky MLB Grant Godfrey made a game-high 15 tackles at Oklahoma. WLB Bo Barnes was not far behind with 10 stops. It has been a season of starts and stops for fifth-year player Alex Afari . The 6-2, 227-pound Cincinnati product is a member of the high school class of 2022 that the NCAA has attempted to exclude from the new 5-for-5 eligibility model. Afari was eligible for UK’s first four games due to a ruling in Jefferson County Circuit Court. However, the NCAA won on appeal at the Kentucky Court of Appeals, making Afari ineligible for the South Carolina and LSU games. A subsequent ruling by the Jefferson County Circuit Court last week restored Afari’s eligibility prior to the Oklahoma contest. The legal back-and-forth “is frustrating for him and for us,” Will Stein said. “We just got to roll with the punches a little bit. It’s out of our control. It’s out of his control at the end of the day, and he’s responded appropriately.” • Vanderbilt WLB Nick Rinaldi is a stat stuffer. A 6-3, 240-pound product of Dover, Massachusetts, Rinaldi has made 42 tackles, 5.5 TFL, 3.5 sacks and has hurried the quarterback four times and broken up passes four times. MLB Bryan Longwell is second on the team with 50 tackles. Longwell had a TFL in Vandy’s rout of UK last season. Advantage : Vanderbilt Defensive backs • Kentucky senior safeties Ty Bryant and Jordan Castell each had two interceptions in the win over Oklahoma. Castell, a 6-2, 211-pound transfer from Florida, foiled a Sooners’ fake field goal with an interception in the end zone and later returned a pick of John Mateer 41 yards for the game’s final touchdown. Bryant, a 6-foot, 196-pound Frederick Douglass High School alumnus, set up Kentucky’s go-ahead TD with a 42-yard interception return, then sealed the Wildcats’ victory with a pick with 21 seconds left in the game. • Vanderbilt strong safety CJ Heard leads the Commodores in tackles with 52. A 5-11, 210-pound Atlanta product who began his college career at Florida Atlantic, Heard also has made four tackles for loss, three sacks, broken up five passes, forced two fumbles and intercepted a pass. Special teams • Kentucky has not had consistently stellar punting in 2026, but Wilson Berry played a big role in the win at Oklahoma. The Australian uncorked a 58-yard, rugby-style kick that backed OU up to its 4-yard line with 2:43 left in the game. On the season, Berry is averaging 44 yards on eight punts and has pinned foes inside their 20-yard line twice. Place-kicker Adam Zouagui is 8 of 11 on field goals in 2026 with a long make of 52 yards. • Vanderbilt punter Tyler Ebel is averaging 47 yards a kick and has pinned opponents inside their 20-yard line on 10 of 27 punts. Place-kicker Brock Taylor is 6 of 8 on field-goal attempts with a long make of 47 yards. For his college career, Taylor is 47 of 53 on field-goal tries with a long make of 57 yards. away.headline: Initial Vanderbilt football injury report before trip to No. 12 Kentucky
away.blurb: Vanderbilt football heads out of town to Lexington, Kentucky this weekend to take on the No. 12 Kentucky Wildcats for its fifth SEC game. But before the game kicks off this weekend, we have to know who is going to be available Saturday night. Wednesday night, the SEC released its initial player availability reports leading up to this weekend’s slate of games. What was not know were the statuses of EDGE Brian Allen Jr., safety Dontae Carter and offensive lineman Mitchell Smith. On the first injury report, Allen Jr. is officially listed as out while Carter is listed as questionable and Smith is listed as probable. Tuesday, Vanderbilt head coach Clark Lea announced that Allen Jr. did not practice due to an ankle injury, but Carter did practice wearing a no-contact jersey. In the case of Smith, Lea sounded hopeful Tuesday that he would be able to play after missing the last two games. In addition to those three, linebacker Josiah Broxton is doubtful for Saturday's game while safety Davin Chandler is listed as questionable. Along with Smith on the probable designation are cornerback Cayden Daniels and defensive lineman Hayden Bray. The Commodores are currently on a four-game losing streak and are the only team in the conference to not win a SEC game this season. Contrast that with Kentucky, who is currently one of the hottest teams in the country and firmly in the College Football Playoff conversation. Vanderbilt had a somewhat lengthy injury report. The Commodores already knew going into the week it was going to be missing backup quarterback Blaze Berlowitz, cornerback Jaylin Lackey, defensive lineman Aaron Bryant and offensive lineman Gunner Givens. In recent weeks, Lea announced season-ending injuries to Givens and Bryant and a collarbone injury to Berlowitz. Vanderbilt will continue to be without linebacker Jamison Curtis, wide receiver Kahden Smith and defensive lineman Nikhil Jefferson Lea will likely give updates on his guys Thursday from tonight's injury report as he usually does. At this point in the year, Vanderbilt is fairly banged up. But it has its final game this weekend before the bye week. This weekend’s game between Vanderbilt and Kentucky is significant to both teams in different ways. One team is looking to get its confidence back while the other is looking to not slip up as a big favorite at home. The Commodores and Wildcats kick off at 6:30 p.m. CT on SEC Network. home.blurb: For Kentucky, linebacker Sam Greene is a significant one to monitor, as he is listed as doubtful. Receiver Nic Anderson is also questionable. Linebacker Grant Grayton is once again listed as out for Saturday's game. Will Stein does not expect it to be a season-long issue. “Not expected to be a season thing, so I'm hoping over the next few weeks we can get him back." The Wildcats will likely get CJ Baxter back ahead of Saturday's matchup, as he is listed as probable, along with linebacker Tavion Wallace. Kentucky football has been pretty banged up on the defensive end lately and were also without starting running back CJ Baxter this past Saturday against Oklahoma. After picking up a gritty win down in Norman, the Wildcats will be taking on a Vandy team that is winless in the SEC through four games, but one that Kentucky can't overlook. As the Wildcats continue to pop up in many playoff projections after yet another win, every single day becomes important if they want to capitalize on a historic start through seven games. Ahead of the matchup with Vandy, here is what the injury report looks like. Earlier this week, Stein made sure his players and fans know to not underestimate what Vandy can do. He isn't paying attention to that 3-4 record next to their name. "I don't think any of us in this room or this organization need to be fooled by any type of record. Last time I checked, (Vandy) embarrassed Kentucky last year and so we know what they are able to do in all three phases." Vandy also features one of the best wide receivers in the country, who is 11th nationally in receiving yards and a massive focal point in how they find success on offense. That, along with Kentucky needing to continue winning to keep their playoff hopes alive are the stories entering this one. The Wildcats can't afford a slip up ahead of a tough stretch to end the season. They'll be facing Vandy mostly healthy on Saturday. What does Kentucky football have to do to achieve its postseason dreams? home.headline: Initial Vanderbilt football injury report before trip to No. 12 Kentucky
home.blurb: Vanderbilt football heads out of town to Lexington, Kentucky this weekend to take on the No. 12 Kentucky Wildcats for its fifth SEC game. But before the game kicks off this weekend, we have to know who is going to be available Saturday night. Wednesday night, the SEC released its initial player availability reports leading up to this weekend’s slate of games. What was not know were the statuses of EDGE Brian Allen Jr., safety Dontae Carter and offensive lineman Mitchell Smith. On the first injury report, Allen Jr. is officially listed as out while Carter is listed as questionable and Smith is listed as probable. Tuesday, Vanderbilt head coach Clark Lea announced that Allen Jr. did not practice due to an ankle injury, but Carter did practice wearing a no-contact jersey. In the case of Smith, Lea sounded hopeful Tuesday that he would be able to play after missing the last two games. In addition to those three, linebacker Josiah Broxton is doubtful for Saturday's game while safety Davin Chandler is listed as questionable. Along with Smith on the probable designation are cornerback Cayden Daniels and defensive lineman Hayden Bray. The Commodores are currently on a four-game losing streak and are the only team in the conference to not win a SEC game this season. Contrast that with Kentucky, who is currently one of the hottest teams in the country and firmly in the College Football Playoff conversation. Vanderbilt had a somewhat lengthy injury report. The Commodores already knew going into the week it was going to be missing backup quarterback Blaze Berlowitz, cornerback Jaylin Lackey, defensive lineman Aaron Bryant and offensive lineman Gunner Givens. In recent weeks, Lea announced season-ending injuries to Givens and Bryant and a collarbone injury to Berlowitz. Vanderbilt will continue to be without linebacker Jamison Curtis, wide receiver Kahden Smith and defensive lineman Nikhil Jefferson Lea will likely give updates on his guys Thursday from tonight's injury report as he usually does. At this point in the year, Vanderbilt is fairly banged up. But it has its final game this weekend before the bye week. This weekend’s game between Vanderbilt and Kentucky is significant to both teams in different ways. One team is looking to get its confidence back while the other is looking to not slip up as a big favorite at home. The Commodores and Wildcats kick off at 6:30 p.m. CT on SEC Network. home.blurb: Kentucky vs. Vanderbilt Injury Report: Sam Greene likely out; CJ Baxter set to play | A Sea Of Blue Skip to main content SB Nation SB Nation logo A Kentucky Wildcats Community A Sea Of Blue October 23, 2026 A Sea Of Blue Notifications Notifications The Feed CJ Baxter is set to make his return for the Kentucky Wildcats, but Same Greene appears unlikely to play. The big news is that standout linebacker Sam Greene is doubtful to play. Greene has played in every game this season after recovering from an ACL tear suffered toward the end of last season. Hopefully, this is not a significant issue and he’ll be able to return coming out of the Wildcats’ Week 9 bye. Running back CJ Baxter, who dressed for the Oklahoma game but was held out, is listed as probable, so he should play. Wide receiver Nic Anderson, who left Saturday’s win in Norman late due to an injury, is listed as questionable, so there’s a 50-50 shot he plays for the time being. Linebacker Tavion Wallace, who’s missed the last three games, tweeted on Wednesday that he’d returned to practice, so that could be a boost to a position that’s been thin. Wallace is officially listed as probable. Fellow linebacker Antawn Smith, who was injured at South Carolina and missed the last two games, has been ruled out for this week. Nearly half the league is down to its backup quarterback, whether due to injury or by choice. The only undefeated team in the conference is UCLA , while Oregon's conference title hopes are hanging on by a thread. Ohio State just picked up a huge win, but faces the prospect of being without Julian Sayin for the rest of the season. It's chaos, and when chaos is around, there's a chance someone unexpected will emerge and take advantage of it. So while No. 16 USC's trip to Madison this weekend to face Wisconsin might not be the headliner game of the weekend, it's a chance for two teams to step forward and stake a claim in the conference. USC has won two straight since dropping a game to Oregon, and perhaps most surprisingly, one of those wins has come on the road. The Trojans are 2-0 outside the Coliseum, which has been a serious problem for them during Lincoln Riley's tenure. Now they're back on the road facing a Wisconsin team coming off its first Big Ten loss at UCLA last week. The winner stays in the Big Ten title race with a chance to capitalize on the chaos. The loser will have to hope for a lot more chaos to befall the rest of the league going forward. USC vs. Wisconsin: Need to know Wisconsin has struggled with USC: They haven't shared a conference for long, but there is familiarity with these programs. Familiarity Wisconsin would sooner forget. USC is 7-1 all time against the Badgers, with the lone loss coming in the 2015 Holiday Bowl. They've only played once as Big Ten foes, and USC won that game 38-21 in Los Angeles during the 2024 season. As for the trip to Camp Randall, USC has won both the games in Madison, though the last meeting came in 1965. NCAA eligibility rules change every day, but I'm pretty sure none of the players who played in that game have remaining eligibility. picks.headline: Three Bold Predictions for Wisconsin's Huge Primetime Clash With No. 16 USC
picks.blurb: Three Bold Predictions for Wisconsin's Huge Primetime Clash With No. 16 USC Skip to main content SI.COM WISCONSIN ATHLETICS FOOTBALL FOOTBALL NEWS SI.COM BADGERS FOOTBALL BASKETBALL NEWS SI.COM BADGERS BASKETBALL Saturday night in Camp Randall Stadium could easily set the tone for the rest of the year for Wisconsin football. A win would instantly erase the pain from Week 7 out in Los Angeles, as it would represent Wisconsin's first victory over a legitimately good opponent and give head coach Luke Fickell another top-20 upset on his resume for the 2026 season, which would go a long way in helping him prove he's the man for the job in Madison. A loss, on the other hand, would even up the Badgers' Big Ten record at 2-2 and set them up with a must-win on Halloween in Iowa City, a situation nobody wants to be in. As Wisconsin continues prep for the Trojans , here's three bold predictions for the Saturday night showdown: Wisconsin shuts down star Trojans' tailback King Miller USC Trojans running back King Miller. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect All week long in the lead-up to UCLA, all we heard about was the Bruins' rugged ground game. A supposedly unstoppable force of nature, headlined by star ball-carrier Wayne Knight, was supposed to run rampant over the Badgers' front seven. All week long in the lead-up to UCLA, all we heard about was the Bruins' rugged ground game. A supposedly unstoppable force of nature, headlined by star ball-carrier Wayne Knight, was supposed to run rampant over the Badgers' front seven. Instead, Wisconsin held the Bruins to 44 rushing yards through the first three quarters (120 after a fourth quarter of mostly clock control from UCLA) while Knight himself posted just 23 yards on 13 carries. All told, UCLA averaged just 3.2 yards per carry. Surprisingly, that didn't matter because the Badgers couldn't contain Bruins' quarterback Ty Dieffenbach, who completed 67% of his passes while tossing for 264 yards. But Wisconsin made a point; even the best rushing attacks in college football should expect to struggle against the Cardinal and White. USC has two very capable backs in King Miller (114 carries, 595 yards, four touchdowns) and Waymond Jordan (63 carries, 287 yards and two scores). However, the Trojans' ground game as a whole ranks just 77th nationally, one spot above the Badgers — both teams run for 152 yards per game. While USC's backs are capable, this isn't the most impressive rushing attack and Wisconsin just proved that it can make even the best ground games in the country struggle mightily. Miller has yet to run for fewer than 45 yards this season; I foresee that happening Saturday night. Colton Joseph takes care of the ball all night Wisconsin Badgers quarterback Colton Joseph. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect After a rough three-interception outing in the upset win over then-No. 13 Penn State, Colton Joseph has taken care of the football, at least through the air. He's lost two fumbles, neither of which were recovered by the defense, but he's also gone two straight games without throwing an interception for the first time in his Badgers career. After a rough three-interception outing in the upset win over then-No. 13 Penn State, Colton Joseph has taken care of the football, at least through the air. He's lost two fumbles, neither of which were recovered by the defense, but he's also gone two straight games without throwing an interception for the first time in his Badgers career. Against USC, there's no reason why he can't make it three. The Trojans have only intercepted three passes this fall across seven games; there's only 11 FBS programs that've played as many games and picked off fewer passes. Their pass defense as a whole has left plenty to be desired; USC is allowing 239 passing yards per game, good for 110th nationally. Joseph has also cut down on the "turnover-worthy plays," according to Pro Football Focus. After he combined for eight over the Badgers' first four games, he has just one over the last two games. The turnover battle is going to be huge in order to pull off an upset like this, but I think Joseph can keep it clean Saturday night. Wisconsin benches PJ Wilkins Wisconsin offensive lineman PJ Wilkins. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect Given how he's played, this wouldn't be a bold prediction under normal circumstances. But the Badgers have insisted on trotting him out there with the starters, and that was painfully clear in Pasadena when they moved Stylz Blackmon to center in place of the injured starter Austin Kawecki, despite the fact that Kawecki's backup Ryan Cory played well in his stead, which also forced Wilkins to start at right guard. He easily "leads" the team with 12 pressures, per Pro Football Focus, although having watched the all-22 tape I'd venture to say that's a generously low estimate. He just doesn't appear to have the quickness to hold up in pass protection. “It’s been a little bit difficult. "We gotta find a way to make sure we have our best five up front every week.” Unfortunately, it's pretty clear the Badgers' "best five" doesn't include Wilkins at this point in time. away.headline: 2 key Badgers remain questionable ahead of Saturday night vs. No. 16 USC
away.blurb: Wisconsin could be about to receive some big-time reinforcements with starting center Austin Kawecki, who's listed on the updated Big Ten injury report as probable for the second straight day. However, two key players remain questionable ahead of the enormous showdown with No. 16 USC . Star cornerback Javan Robinson, who's been lights out for the Badgers in coverage this fall, remains questionable along with wideout Malachi Coleman, who's arguably Wisconsin's most explosive and dangerous receiver. Two running backs are also included on the report for Wisconsin. Nate Palmer, who has just nine carries for 26 yards this season, is listed as questionable. That's not the biggest cause for concern, as when starter Abu Sama has been healthy, he's the Badgers' RB4 behind Sama, Darrion Dupree and Bryan Jackson. But speaking of Dupree, he also popped up on the injury report, albeit in the "probable" category. If Robinson is unavailable, that could spell trouble for a Wisconsin secondary that looked surprisingly permeable against UCLA backup quarterback Ty Dieffenbach. As I've written previously , this isn't the right week to have concerns in you rsecondary or about your pass coverage; Trojans' quarterback Jayden Maiava is No. 2 nationally in passing yards with 2,045. As for Coleman, his absence would hurt Wisconsin as well. His speed and ability to stretch defenses vertically can create all kinds of problems if he's utilized correctly. No other Wisconsin wideout has shown the ability to consistently beat defensive backs downfield. If he's indeed unavailable, expect Jaylon Domingeaux, who made his Badgers' debut in Pasadena, to take on a bigger role. Kawecki is dealing with a broken hand, as Fickell revealed at his post-game press conference following the defeat at UCLA. Considering the head coach had previously stated the ailment was to Kawecki's right hand (his snapping hand), it's fair to wonder how he could slide back into his starting center spot with that kind of injury. Could Wisconsin keep Stylz Blackmon at center and insert Kawecki in at right guard so he can still play without having to actually grip the ball? What Wisconsin's injury updates mean While we're familiar with the nature of Kawecki's injury, it's unclear what Robinson and Coleman are dealing with. It is worth noting that Robinson played his third-fewest snaps of the season at the Rose Bowl with just 55. In the Badgers' first two Big Ten games, he played 66 snaps against Penn State and 71 snaps against Michigan State. If Robinson can't play, Eric Fletcher Jr would most likely get the start in his stead opposite Jai'mier Scott. MADISON — The Wisconsin Badgers stumbled and fell last week at UCLA. They now have a new opportunity to right the ship this Saturday at home versus No. 16 USC. The Badgers (4-2, 2-1 Big Ten) struggled on offense last Saturday against the Bruins, only mustering 214 yards of total offense and seven points compared to UCLA’s 384 yards and 17 points. This weekend’s game against the Trojans (6-1, 3-1 Big Ten) presents a whole new set of challenges for UW. USC has had a strong start to their Big Ten season, with their only blemish on the year coming at home to the Oregon Ducks. Since then, the Trojans have rattled off back-to-back one-score wins over the likes of Washington and Penn State, sending USC slowly but surely up the AP Top 25 rankings. USC’s offense is led by Heisman hopeful Jayden Maiava, who actively ranks second in the nation in passing yards (2,045) while also ranking fourth in the country in passing touchdowns (18) this year. It also helps that Maiava has Elijah Paige, one of the nation’s top left tackles, protecting his blind side. Despite the level of talent scattered throughout the USC offense, the Badger defense has proven time and time again that it can match up with some of the nation’s best offenses. Wisconsin ranks 16th in the country in total yards allowed/game (286.7) while also being the sixth-hardest defense to pass against in the NCAA in terms of passing efficiency. Saturday’s game marks yet another tough test for a Badger team that is on the second of what will likely end up being three-straight weeks of ranked matchups. Next week, the Badgers travel to Iowa City to take on the currently ranked Iowa Hawkeyes.
